n: LNG Market Report
x: As we publish the energy major Total is performing its remote investor day with a very central focus on the environment and a transition to a less carbon intensive future. At the same time prominent news stories portray that traders are also accelerating their transition to renewables.   It’s this transition that relevance to LNG really starts to take hold and should give some comfort to the average reader of this weekly publication - LNG currently has a very significant role to play. Global LNG demand might be taking a pause whilst celebrations are enjoyed for China’s Golden week but weather systems such as ‘La Nina’ are predicted to bring colder temperatures in due course adding to increasing market demand. On the flip side, supply is subject to significant interruptions across the global with the latest in Norway at the Hammerfest plant, thankfully no injuries, but production is not expected to return until November.  More specifically and to LNGC’s, interruptions, increased demand and illiquidity of vessels combines to create a very intriguing market, consequences could result in muted activity but could also cause significant opportunity for freight to rise to year highs as schedules change and ton time increases as vessel head further afield. Naysayers will point to high European storage levels and the lack of global industrial production as everyone tousles with the pandemic. It won’t change overnight and we don’t expect great changes in levels this week but next week may bring more clarity and improved owner returns. In the meantime we would like to wish all those who are celebrating Golden week a pleasant and restful break.

x: AMERICAS The US propane supply is in very good shape heading into this Winter. In fact, with domestic storages at tank tops, if it is not a cold winter, the market will shift from comfortable to long. However,  what the traders are now concentrating on is the next winter. The generally feeling is that although this winter should be fine, the winter 2021/2022 looks very tight. International demand is growing at a rate that surpasses US production growth and in order to keep the world supplied, US exports will need to be at maximum levels. How this effects the relative price is what traders are trying to decipher but it looks certain exports will maintain at terminal capacity. In South America, the Brazilians have remained active despite their winter season winding down and we look to the other South American importers to begin contemplating the sale of their imports into the Northern Hemisphere winter markets.

We have seen an increase in prompt availability, predominately sublets from portfolio players and traders, emerged in the market as a result of the disruptions caused by the hurricane. x: AMERICAS: The weekly EIA propane inventory report  showed an unexpectedly high build of 4.389mmbbls, from 90.833mmbbls for the week ending 21 Aug 2020 to 95.222mmbbls as of 20 Aug 2020.  The data also revealed a YOY increase of 2.366mmbbls when comparing the Aug 2020 figures to the Aug 2019 data.  Most of the build occurred in PADD III (Gulf Coast) and is reckoned to be the result of lifting delays as related to the passing of Hurricane Laura.  On that, the only terminal to be directly impacted – and which continues to suffer closure – is the LoneStar facility at Nederland, TX.  Where the Houston Ship Channel and Freeport, TX terminals were temporarily closed (and briefly, at that), the Category 4 storm made landfall only slightly East of the Sabine River and caused significant damage in its wake, and left the LoneStar terminal out of commission for approximately a week.  Front-month Mont Belvieu values are presently hovering in the 49ctgs/gal range but then rise through the balance of the year, only tapering, presumably, on seasonality factors at end Q1 2021.  With US stock levels having risen so sharply at the end of August the sentiment is one of cautious optimism in that it appears at present to be sufficient volumes to satisfy both domestic res/com and petrochemical-related demand and export volumes.  But with near record-level exports seen in August, and concern of production declines, the underlying concern of insufficient stocks lingers and is thus supportive of the pricing structure for the next 4-5 months.

x: AMERICAS: Discussion this week have been centred around Hurricane Laura which made landfall Wednesday evening between Texas and Louisiana. From reports this morning it seems the hurricane bypassed Houston and the ship channel. Enterprise expect 1.5 days of delay due to ship channel closures. Nederland, which was in the path of the storm has avoided major damage and, after a coast guard survey, expect 1 day of delay. We expect this news to assuage fears of long delays. The 1.5 million barrel build in US inventories has now pushed stocks up to 90.8 million barrels. With domestic production stronger than originally expected, traders believe there will be enough product to sustain winter demand and exports. The more pressing question in today’s market is when will we start to see global winter demand?

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It has been a rather turbulent week in the LNG market, as commodity prices have seen almost roller-coasterly up and down movements, spot shipping rates have stormed upwards and last, but unfortunately not the least, there is a major hurricane (Hurricane Laura) about to make a landfall near Texas-Louisina coaster border, consequently threatening to shut down a chunk of US LNG production at least temporarily. Spot shipping market has remained active, mainly driven by multiple spot requirements from the East of Suez, resulting into a rather slim prompt tonnage availability, quite surprisingly for this time of the year. That said, the West of Suez have also had its’ fair share of interest for tonnage, but notably with delivery windows a bit further ahead, perhaps in the hopes of capturing the best potential contango window before the Northern Hemisphere winter starts. The shipping market definitely feels strongly buoyant in the near-term, but there is still some uncertainty whether this heightened sentiment can be supported over the shoulder months, which only time will tell for certain. From the newbuilding front, it has been reported that Smart LNG has finalized agreements to order additional ten Arc7 LNG carriers from Zvezda Shipbuilding Complex in Russia, for the upcoming Arctic LNG 2 project. Furthermore, there are also quite a few S&P transactions circulating in the market.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Sentiments picked up over the last few days as demand and enquiries for shipping increases due to the anticipation of winter demand for gas. Despite the apparent long list of available vessels, proposals for vessels with compliant specifications and available periods come far and few in between. Portfolio players and projects are constantly having to optimise their fleet schedules in order to offer their vessels to charterers’ requirements, clearly indicating there is not many vessels to choose from which are readily available. It may not be a good time to be short shipping going forward as availabilities change on a daily basis. Both basins have seen enquiries for the months of September, October and November deliveries. Charters for inter-basin trades could be revived in the next weeks or so, which would soak up shipping even more. Charter rate ideas have generally been far apart between owners and charterers, and it may continue to be the case as shipowners stand firm on their commercial expectations.   Brace yourselves, winter is coming.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The LNG market has slowly started “getting into shape” for winter, with sentiment gradually increasing. A couple of multi-month shipping requirements have been covered and spot interest remains active,  increasing spot rates. Asia delivered LNG price has further improved, opening a handful of potential opportunities for traders and portfolio players. Availability of vessels has seen a slight decrease, yet there remains an overhang of tonnage to work through, still with Charterers’ seeking coverage for future laycans while Owner’s attention is focused on prompt. On the flip side, concerns over a second wave of coronavirus could put a halt to recent improving sentiments, as a number of countries are monitoring recent upticks in infection levels. Nevertheless, for the time being, Owners are holding a firm stance on their ideas for winter. In the Newbuilding market no new orders have been reported this week.

With these high inventories, one would expect Mt Belvieu to be below 52% of WTI as it is today. The netback picture is not pretty from the US at the moment. The arb for September could support US FOB bids in the 4cpgs around cancellation levels. However the physical window discount in the East is keeping firm bids from being shown. We expect to see an improvement in netback values if any positive demand signals are seen from the East. If this occurs at the same time as a drop in Mt Belvieu and cheaper freight rates, the netback value could see a sharp rise. Let’s hope this occurs sooner rather than later.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: August is here and the ‘holiday season’ feels quite different. Uncertainty of recent months has only been exacerbated by the continued worries around a potential second wave of coronavirus in Europe and the ongoing depth and breadth of the first wave in the US and this goes to reflect why activity and winter sentiment is more muted this year compared to previous ones.    Governments and advisory firms are more openly starting to question if the recovery will be a more of a ‘U’ than the ‘V’ that was touted in earlier predictions, but no one really knows, so for the time being risk by the majority is been minimized and this leaves shipping floundering. European storage inventories act as a good indicator to the glut that is upon the industry reaching 86% capacity earlier this week compared to a 5 year average of 70%, could this trigger the need for floating storage? This week North Asia prices extended their recent rally which follow similar gains in Europe and North America, so although LNG is abundant there are improving signals ahead of winter. Availability in all basins remains sufficient yet laycans remain frustratingly distant and economically undesirable for owners sitting prompt. In short, let the holiday season pass and bring on winter.   In the new building market Shell has signed separate agreements for two LNG ships each with Knutsen LNG, Korea Line and ICBC Financial Leasing and institutional investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management.

t: LNG Market Report

x: Voyage economics remain broadly flat this week, but the sense of a firming shipping market is growing. Prompt business is still dominated by spot cargoes and tender-driven enquiries, and this continues to churn through the availability list without reducing it much. Looking ahead though, sublets are being withdrawn and the bid / offer spread is finally converging, giving hope to owners seeking to salvage something of the year. It's now a question of timing: the best cargo economics span roughly October to December, but owners are reluctant to risk this much idle time prior to delivery, so few multimonth fixtures have been concluded. As the weeks roll on and owners get more visibility of their fleet schedules, we expect a flurry of these fixtures. This has not been a normal year, but despite the disruption of recent months it's reassuring to see the familiar dance of owners and charterers as we look towards winter. No newbuildings reported this week and prices remain flat.

Fixing levels aren’t yet showing sharp increases while the tonnage is there to meet demand, although ships are slowly trickling into employment and sublets are being reabsorbed back into their portfolios. While most firm activity has been east of Suez, the Atlantic market is being watched carefully; after a very weak summer, expectations of an improving LNG trading environment appear to be bearing fruit as early estimates suggest September US Gulf cargo cancellations are down considerably. With players seeking winter coverage and the window for September spot chartering approaching, we could see sentiment firm up in the basin. No Newbuilds have been ordered this week but interest in projects and small scale seems to be restarting, with the Philippines moving forward with FSRU talks, Mozambique LNG project getting financed and the Qatar expansion progressing. As parts of the world re-emerge from lockdown and some limited cross-border travel returns, a sense of normality is returning. Wherever you are in the world, stay safe and we hope that your 2020 will perk up soon enough.

Similarly, forward fixing levels for both Owners and Charterers are not aligned.  Ideas on floating storage plays for winter deliveries have also encouraged multi month discussions to resurfaced again as there could be some potential upside in a trade, storing now and selling into the later part of the year.   Market participants are also keenly awaiting news on the amount of US cargo cancellations for September as that would either increase or decrease demand for shipping.  Newbuilding prices remain unchanged and there were no further reports of any new large LNG carrier orders this week. With upcoming LNG projects currently in yard discussions, we could see a spur in newbuilding orders over the second half of 2020.

Furthermore, independent owners with open winter tonnage are growing increasingly selective on which opportunities they will entertain. It’s almost mythical how these things tend to come together around week 27 every year. One thing does seem certain, and that is that the market may have bottomed out…although this does not mean that we’ll see a sudden increase in spot rates this side of the summer holidays.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: There are plenty of permutations of possible events that could greatly influence the LNG shipping market in the months to come. Vessel availability at the moment is high, as expected as per the seasonal lack of gas demand during summer months where utility players generally have pockets of availability of sublets. This, further fuelled by cargo cancellations in the United States due to the drop of LNG demand caused by COVID-19 lockdowns, led to US lifters’ vessels being available in the spot market. Longer voyages are expected by the LNG fleet dedicated to LNG exporters when long term buyers defer the receipt of cargoes to manage their inventory levels, which could absorb shipping capacities but these have not been sufficient to manage the long tonnage situation. Geo-political events could yet again be the catalyst for volatile swings in shipping rates as international disputes could lead to possible sanctions, blockades, et cetera. While further progress on treatments and vaccines for COVID-19 could lead to added confidence on lifting of lockdowns worldwide, which could lead to rise in LNG demand. These are unpredictable times but as for this week, rates and sentiments remain flat.  No newbuilding orders to report this week.

This rise in production is already having an effect as export volumes are beginning to ramp from the US East Coast. With global demand starting to recover and US production rising traders are reluctant to cancel US cargoes. Lets hope both these trends continue and keep cancellations at bay. t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Global markets have gradually started their recovery, although improvements in the LNG market are likely to lag a little as product prices and shipping rates remain flat across the board. Shipping availability is slowly building into July, and in anticipation of US cargo cancellations a rather tough environment exists in the prompt market. The current bid/ask spread remains relatively wide, making transactions challenging as Owners and Charterers expectations remain somewhat disconnected. Nevertheless, there is some optimism looking further ahead to autumn and winter. A West-to-East arbitrage and contango pricing may result in a stronger cargo market, where ship owners and players long tonnage may see some profitable opportunities.    On the Newbuilding front, again there have been no new large LNG vessel orders to report this week or this year, and we may end up with no new orders to report for first half 2020!

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: General news flows in recent weeks have had an air of pessimism but the mood may be changing, with countries reopening and an expectation that things are starting to look a little brighter and the same can be said for the LNG industry. Despite low product prices and LNGC rates, the industry continues to its forward progress. The 19.2 billion US dollar shipbuilding deal agreed last week by Qatar Petroleum with three South Korean yards offer Owners a well needed distraction from today’s spot market.  New areas and sectors of demand is also bearing fruit, with further LNG bunkering vessels being launched.  And whilst operating on the open seas has seen new challenges raised through the restrictions on movement of personal and quarantine measures, MAN dual-fuel engines passed one million operating hours this year, which reflects a level of experience and operating history that should offer improved reliability and a greater understanding of the technology meaning smoother sailing for Owners and Charterers alike. All we need next is a sustainable arbitrage to reduce what is a slightly bulging availability list.

As it stands, US inventories now rest at a similar level to this time last year, though the sentiment of considerable Q3 and Q4 product tightness remains throughout the market. t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As prompt LNG trading and shipping conditions continue to underwhelm, most market players are busy making the best of things today while looking ahead for hints of change. The bare facts are that LNG pricing remains low across the globe, US cargo cancellations are biting and vessel availability is creeping up. But if these pessimal conditions are the harshest for survival they’re also a great driver of ideas and innovation, and as we enter the second half of the year there are increasing signs of clever thinking and smart trades. High inventory levels and low pricing in Europe combined with fewer US cargoes is creating a novel dynamic in the north Atlantic, and demand continues to return to markets in the east as economies gain momentum emerging from lockdown. The prospect of European reloads to capture value either in localised contangoes or in inter-basin trade are encouraging for tonne-time and tonne-mile demand, and in turn ship owners are entertaining creative ideas on rates such floating structures. There will be some fascinating moves in the months ahead.   Although no newbuildings have been ordered this week, Qatar Petroleum have moved to reserve berths for more than 100 LNGCs at the three main Korean yards.

Netbacks remain around 4 cpg however deals continue to be done above these levels as buyers seem to be more content on moving their vessels as opposed to netback econs. If not for crashing freight rates (Houston-Chiba last done at $67/ton on Wednesday and now being discussed at USD 60/mt)  it is likely we would have seen June cargo cancellations from the US Gulf-though none have been reported as of yet. A lot of talk in the US propane market is orbiting around considerable product tightness come the end of 3q and 4q of 2020. Covid related demand lapses have led to considerable cutbacks on the part of crude producers in the Marcellus, Uttica, Permian and Midland basins. Some 600mb/d of production have been cutback this month-as producers wait for demand in Jet fuel, motor oil and other crude demand drivers to wake back up before turning the tap back on. As we are still building inventories, per usual this time of year, the propane production cutbacks are not yet felt in full force although there are certainly warning lights flashing.

t: LNG Market Report

x: Spot shipping rates are mostly unchanged from last week and sentiment remains soft. Another round of US cargo cancelations, although perhaps not as large as some participants feared, has nonetheless dampened hopes of an improved summer market. Some charterers are testing the market for opportunities to take winter coverage at reduced rates. However, as of this week, there exists a stand-off with independent owners reluctant to fix the traditionally stronger winter months in today’s soft market. While there aren’t many encouraging signs for owners in the immediate future, cautious optimism will endure as uncertainty hangs over second half of the year. Much will depend on the cargo market and in particular regional gas pricing; for example, high gas storage and low pricing in Europe may support the emergence of reloads. While this might not support the levels seen in recent winters, it would be an encouraging sign for utilisation.   Again, no large LNG newbuilding orders to report this week, but DSME did report a notable large Q-Max type FSRU by a Far East owner for German terminal project. There are also a few second-hand transactions in the pipeline.

x: It has been another monotonous week for the LNG Shipping market. Sentiments continue to dip further amid signs of limited demand in both basins. The vast number of cancellations on cargoes to be delivered in June from US projects and what seems like an unending closed arbitrage trading window have led to a lack of opportunities for shipping and rather, more sublets seen in the market. The shipping rates is still under pressure as “last done” were reportedly concluded lower week on week. Nevertheless, we do see some premium on the larger sizes, as more end users look to take advantage of the low LNG spot prices to procure larger quantities. Furthermore, there are discussions with some players interested in securing multi months at the current levels, for prompt to Q3 2020 delivery and for periods up till the end of next winter season. While the present environment is challenging, if the ongoing lock-downs and restrictions in most parts of the world eases, we could see the global energy demand pick up and LNG demand to follow. On the Newbuilding front, there hasn’t been any firm deals concluded last week and sentiment remains steady to soft.

x: The inertia of last week’s shipping market continued at the start of this one, as a lack of fresh activity held the market in a slight limbo. The cargo market has only seen a modest improvement in Asia: Japanese inventory levels are now nearing capacity, and with plenty of cargo already on the water, we're likely to see an increase in floating activity over the next few weeks. However, with a healthy tonnage list in the Pacific well into July, rates continue to trickle off. The Atlantic is showing a softening market for intra-basin trade, with sentiment falling and uncertainty on the cargo side. Conversely, ships moving East with US Gulf spot cargoes are still fixing at last-done levels. Multi month enquiries are becoming a hot topic as some charterers look at taking coverage in this seasonally soft market. Looking ahead, there are still plenty of unanswered questions caused by the pandemic that will have an impact on LNG trades and LNG shipping for the rest of the year: dry docking schedules, SIRE inspections, crew changes to name but a few and it's not until countries and travel arrangements begin to return to the 'new normal' that these will be answered. No newbuild orders seen to be placed at Shipyards this week, despite economics in favour of the buyer. We have therefore kept newbuild prices stable.

x: It has been a slightly quieter week as we have been enjoying several public holidays across the globe (namely Labour Day holidays and the Golden Week in Japan) giving the markets a short breather. Moreover, based on the news this week, the Covid19 – situation might find a bit more light at the end of the tunnel, as various countries have slowly released their plans for lifting some of the ongoing restrictions. This is cautiously positive news for the global economy and energy demand, but the road to recovery is still very uncertain. The same fundamentals apply to the world of LNG, where the supply overhang is still very much a fundamental problem causing bearish views for the rest of the year for both cargo volume and shipping. That said, we have seen a bit more interest in multimonth TC-periods as Charterers’ and Owners’ ideas on expected rate levels have narrowed. This might be more speculative than purely demand driven, but nonetheless seeing more term activity is a good sign. In the spot market, we are recording a small softening on the rate levels this week, as the ongoing charter interest, which is mainly driven by various spot cargo tenders, is not enough to compensate for the lengthy vessel availability list. Finally, there has been no new large LNGC orders reported this week (and orders for first 5 months 2020 are down by 12 units compared to 2019). With a strong US dollar, low interest rates and limited new orders from other shipping segments, there could be a risk of softening newbuilding prices.

t: LNG Market Report

x: “COVID-19” has been a consistent feature in our weekly reports lately, as the impact of the pandemic is evident on LNG and LNG shipping. LNG prices are undoubtedly kept at low levels due to the glut of LNG cargoes. While the summer months are traditionally with the weakest LNG demand for the year, this year comes with the added element of pandemic-induced bearishness. One may expect muted activity but this is actually far from what we observe. Vessels are being fixed in both basins, many on the back of cargo tenders or spare cargoes on offer from producers, seemingly due to cargo deferments from long term buyers. LNG prices from the long term contracts are higher priced compared to reported spot prices, providing portfolio players the opportunities to acquire FOB cargoes at low prices to fill these high-priced shorts, which is leading to vessel enquiries for optimisation.

While exports decreased this week compared to last, it’s reported that 1.15 million barrels /day found their way to the water, furthering the notion that propane and butane has been far less susceptible to coronavirus demand interruptions than rest of the barrel. In the recent weeks, the propane price along with Spot cargo discussion has been kept afloat by considerable demand from China, Indonesia, Korea, Japan and India. Indias demand for LPG has increased as much as 20 percent, and will keep exports firm if it continues.  As it turns out, the US is no different. Argus reported that domestic propane marketers saw 10 percent increase in usage this month compared to last- contributing to balance. In the US Gulf, terminals and third party sellers are looking to market the remaining 2-3 May cargos, before looking ahead to June. As it stands levels for these cargos are being valued at 6-7  cpg , with ship availability proving the difficult variable.

x: Implications of Covid-19 continue to affect global markets as demand keeps plummeting worldwide. Oil is trading at remarkably low levels, and whilst the oil price contango has a positive impact on tanker rates due to storage, when it comes to LNG the scenario is different. Cargo prices have remained soft and shipping rates may see further pressure as vessel availability increases in both basins. As was widely anticipated, a significant number of cargoes for June loading in the US have been cancelled leaving excess shipping length from portfolio players, utilities and traders. In this environment we could see further rate drops as talks on potential production cuts continue. On the operational side, vessel discharges, Dry docks and quarantine restrictions have caused uncertainties in availability amongst market participants and one could argue that we might see sporadic upticks on the back of these disruptions. Only time will tell as economies start recovering, but there is no doubt we anticipate a bumpy ride in the months to come. In the Newbuilding market, it was reported today that Qatar Petroleum signed a Deed of Agreement with Chinese yard Hudong- Zhonghua to reserve yard capacity for upto 16 vessels of 174,000 cbm for delivery 2024 and 2025, and with options into 2026.

x: AMERICAS: April is shaping up to be a record setting month for exports from the US. This large export program coupled with the reduced imports from Canada has extended the demand season for propane.  Normally by the end of March builds are seen in the inventories but that is not the case this year, even with daily production being sustained over the 2 million barrels per day. With the strong exports, freight has made a recovery, which is putting pressure on the arb, but strong worldwide demand seems poised to keep arb open. In the Southern hemisphere seasonal demand is coming into play with Petrobras becoming an active buyer for US cargos and other buyers preparing to do the same.

t: LNG Market Report

x: Owners and charterers have had to respond quickly and aggressively in some instances to the pandemic that continues to effect the global markets. The response has varied but generally we have seen the emergence of a two-tier market over the past couple of weeks. In one camp, and reflected in the reductions in headline rate in our weekly report, are the owners and disponent owners seeking coverage and utilisation for their fleet; in the other camp are the owners who remain firmer, in anticipation of a tighter market due to the disruption to fleet schedules, delays in discharging and in project maintenance, and in quarantine measures requiring set periods between port calls. With such distinct views and limited depth to the market, there is considerable volatility at present. This may subside as the fixing period moves into June, when the possibility of cargo cancellations and the potential for vessel availability to grow could have an impact on the shipping market. On a separate note no new orders have been placed, as one would expect and new build prices take a small decline, as do second-hand prices.

Despite the premium softening to 30ish level into India and Indonesia this week, the household demands from both regions continuously lend support to the EAST market. India has announced further lockdown and players expect its June purchase requests. Indonesia Pertamina issued several tenders this week to secure evenly split cargos from End May to July delivery, with requests on fixed price for June/July tons. Taiwan CPC issued buy tender for end May/early June 11/11 but limited offers received.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Export cargos from the US continue, despite cratering worldwide oil demand. In fact we expect the exports to continue thru 2020 and April is on track to be the largest month so far this year. Ironically the falling oil demand has actually increased worldwide lpg demand due to refinery lpg being virtually eliminated. A twist few expected when the economy came to a halt a mere three weeks ago. With the demand side holding, the next question is on the supply.  Production had already decreased and many are now waiting to see if there will be a new OPEC which might include US producers. Propane inventories fell 156,000 barrels this week but still remain well above 2019 levels.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market

As expected, C3/C4 spread has enlarged to $20, due to the robust prompt demand from India.  FOB discussions varied widely as bid idea at small premium while seller targets at double digits. The sole support on premium lies in the consistency of India purchase, which remains a question for forwarding months. Despite active bids at FEI plus teens in window, sellers are keener to sell cargos into China. As FEI/CP spread narrowed down within $10 only whilst landed price into China for May arrival at May CP plus low 40ish, weakening but still more economic.   Several Indian tenders were awarded with CFR price ranging from CP plus 40s to 80s reportedly, relating on exact laycan/laytime requests and other conditions. This week BPCL issued buy tender again to secure another 90k tones for May to early June delivery. Indonesia Pertamina was reported to award one evenly split cargo for May delivery in last tender, and this week issued new tender for another cargo in June delivery.   Deals into China recently are mainly driven by petchem feedstock demand. One Schina-based PDH closed their tender to secure 23kt propane delivered in last decade May. Meanwhile, at the time of writing, two more PDH users have tendered to buy total up-to two full propane cargos from mid-May to 1h June delivery.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Another week of uncertainty has passed, with various schemes and scenarios stretching out like a river delta for the coming months, and owners and charterers face decisions today armed with an incomplete picture of an unknown future. The cargo market remains soft, and following several force majeure events and high inventory levels one might fear the worst; however, trading uncertainty has led to some increased tonne-time, and travel restrictions may cause some terminal operators and ship owners to defer maintenance to later in the year. Amidst this, the cargoes have kept coming…so far. Availability has broadly kept pace with fresh requirements, so rates and voyage economics are holding firm, albeit with some froth. Further out, an array of factors muddy the pitch even more: the persistence or otherwise of COVID-19; the continued level of production out the US Gulf; the pace of demand growth as different economies begin their recoveries at different times and at different rates; rescheduled terminal maintenance hitting LNG supply as we enter winter; a possible tightening of the shipping market if a surge of vessels head in for dry dock…as we move through the year, only one thing appears certain: nobody will get every call correct. Yard activity has been quiet, with no new orders placed this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market

The prompt demand from India due to lockdown, and the slow recovery from China demand, both somehow lends supports to it. May CP is traded at $235 at the time being, but it is yet too early to say whether it can stand firm amid this volatile market. But due to the prompt demand on evenly split cargos, C3/C4 spread is traded at $18 now, wider than Apr and expected to enlarge continuously.    FAR EAST:  The week is dominant by tenders from India and Indonesia. Indonesia Pertamina also tendered to buy one equal ratio cargos for 2h Apr or May arrival. Late last week a couple of propane cargos were sold at May CP plus 40ish into China. But this week sellers target for higher level, as other market demand spiked up with anticipation for less supply on May arrival due to some cancellations for Apr liftings ex US.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The volatility in energy markets around the world is keeping traders busy as they try to capitalise on an open arbitrage or other fluctuations in product prices. This is in turn leading to a “stop/start” LNG shipping market, where market participants are constantly evaluating their options to either add tonnage or sublet depending on the latest price movements and trading opportunities. The end of last week saw positive momentum in the shipping market, but as the arbitrage closed so did charterers interest in tonnage and activity quietened down again. Subsequently, rates have come off a little from last week. Charterers appear to be looking at multi-month business a little earlier this year than last, although competition between owners remain strong. No new orders or 2nd hand transactions since last report.    We hope all are in good health during this challenging time. Stay safe!

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: With all the changes in the world over the last fea weeks, two big questions are hanging over the US markets:  1.	Will there be enough supply to keep the mt Belvieu Price of propane and butane to support exports ? 2.	Will there be enough international demand to support the exports if the product and price maintain reasonable levels ?  We feel the answers to both are supportive for US exports. Firstly, we do not expect the cheap crude markets to maintain beyond the Summer and within this time frame,  we expect producers to maintain current production levels. Current economics will prevent growth,  but maintaining current levels , can and will support exports. As far as international pull on US product, we feel this will be there as well. Possibly for different reasons than usual but there none the less.  US inventories ended the demand season at 64 million barrels , a figure which is 21 million barrels above last year. The arb , a bit all over the place, seems to be maintaining above cancellation economics , which is certainly good news for all.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market

Some players do not favor a super-duper cheap CP to cause huge inventory loss.   One trading house issued semi-term buy tender for one equal ratio cargo monthly from Jun to Dec lifting. Chinese importers are also actively buying 2H Apr to May delivered cargos lately, with some deals concluded at the premium over $40 and few equal ratio buyers remaining. One SChina PDH user issued tender to buy 22kt C3 for 8-16th May delivery. Other PDH users are also inquiring for May arrival propane for feedstocks. Taiwan CPC issued buy tender to secure one 11/11 delivered during 3st to 12rd May, and the tender is still in validity. Indonesia tendered promptly to buy one equal ratio cargo for 19-21 Apr delivery, and the result is yet to know.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market

Understandable when Mt Belvieu propane prices have been relatively strong compared to crude (although at 20 year lows on flat price) while delivered markets weak. The seventh consecutive draw in US inventories of 1.8 million barrels was larger than expected and did not help. The effect has been USGC FOB market is cancellations. Rumoured between seven and ten VLGCs for April. The hope is that these cancellations will build inventories, bearish Mt Belvieu, widening the arb. The dampener could be new bearish propane production estimates for 2020-2021 in this new ultra-low crude price environment.  Leading to traders asking themselves if the arb will widen as hoped, and if so when?

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The commodity and financial markets across the globe have been nothing less than volatile, no different to what the LNG shipping markets have experienced of late. The LNG shipping spot market activities went into overdrive in the Atlantic with a series of vessel requirements issued, along with  a flurry of spot fixtures and vessel swaps, as sentiment spiked amongst the shipowners and players with relets. These are spilling over to the Pacific market where intra-Asia chartering requirements began to emerged. Vessels are available for shipowners to propose to these requirement, however with increased rate expectations as compared to just a week ago.  As many of us work from homes during these unprecedented times, the lockdowns, quarantines and border closures have proved to provide a challenge to the shipping operations and crew management efforts. We spare a thought to all seafarers who have been affected during this period.  No LNG vessel newbuild orders or 2nd hand transactions were reported last week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: In the midst of another tumultuous week in global trade the EIA reported a draw of 310,000 barrels, slightly below what was predicted. The news did little to affect the US propane market which had already plummeted in parity with international declines, on the back of crude. As it stands, the April/May arb and netbacks sit at around $112/ton and 4 cents/gallon respectively. With that said, discussion for spot cargos has not completely dissipated. Logic being that as daily life heads in the direction of normalcy in China, the demand PDH and petchem feed stock will once again require tons from the US. The discussion that many contact holders are currently having is whether the economics dictate to cancel cargos, pending agreed upon fee, and buy from the spot market. This equation has kept activity buoyed, at least for the time being.  Remarkably, Mt Belvieu Non-Tet propane stands at 61.14% WTI and has crossed the below 30cpg for the first time since Jan 17th 1999.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: With ongoing events affecting most of the global economic markets, LNG shipping firmed up this week. Rates in the Atlantic have turned and we’re now seeing an uptick, and although the Pacific didn’t see quite the gains that the Atlantic did due to prompt tonnage still lingering in the basin, fundamentals are growing stronger and the floor feels like it has been found for now. Sentiment from Owners is likely to rally off the back of stronger voyage economics, but the requirements are needed to back this up: the Atlantic was supported by a spate of enquires for US Gulf cargoes while the Pacific was a little quieter. On the cargo side, China is likely to need higher imports in the short term as the country begins its recovery, as many head back to work and industrial demand increases. This could see growth in spot opportunities over the next couple of months. One growing concern though, is that with China now appearing to recover from COVID-19, could we see the country impose restrictions on inbound trade from regions with ongoing infections? There were no newbuilding orders this week but yard prices have come down reflecting a strong US Dollar. Staying with the yards we’ve yet to see the full impact of the ongoing situation: disruption to supply chains and workplace restrictions put in place for the yard workers, there may be delays to deliveries ahead. With COVID-19 now affecting most of the globe, we hope that you and your families, and those of the seafarers we rely on across all sectors, all stay safe and healthy.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It has been one of the most dramatic weeks in the history of oil & gas industry, of which we and other market players are still trying to grasp what the real ramifications might be for the LNG markets. The oil price crash and wildly spreading Covid-19 virus have left many wondering what the rest of the year might entail and how one can adjust their forward views amidst this volatility and uncertainty. That said, the LNG shipping market had a surprisingly active week, with multiple spot and multi-month opportunities emerging, the latter being clearly incentivized by softening rate levels for 6-12 month time charters. One could describe this “multi-month hunting” almost an annual phenomenon taking place in around March-May when the final winter activity has bypassed and owners are struggling get good utilization in the spot market. However, this year it all feels a bit different, as the unpredictability of LNG prices, cargo flows and shipping rates seems to be influencing market players to hedge their bets and choose utilization over speculation. To sum up, we are keeping spot rates mostly unchanged this week, but have adjusted our term rates across the line. From the newbuilding front, we have no new orders to report this week, but yard prices in general are slightly softening as US dollar strengthens.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market

x: AMERICAS: Mt Belvieu propane has not been falling as fast as global propane markets, or even crude oil markets for that matter. Non-TET propane now lies at 46.8% WTI. This has closed the arbs East and West, and although freight has been coming off helping netbacks slightly , we are now in cargo cancellation territory. The 2.9 million barrel draw for the week ending March 6th was the 5th consecutive draw in inventories which is not unusual for winter however in this new era of mega production we had become used to  Winter inventory builds. With the current oil price war going on there have been worries of shrinking domestic oil and gas production through 2020. US companies already in danger to survive might be forced into bankruptcy with WTI crude in the high 20’s  and Natural Gas well below 2.00 / mcf.  Many have a view that 100 million barrels in inventories by the start of the 2020 draw season (October 1,2020) are needed to sustain new export capacity and US winter demand. These factors are lending strength to the Mt Belvieu propane market, and the question is will cancellations in April be needed to weaken Mt Belvieu and reopen the arb.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The current market remains rather bearish with shipping rates seen dipping week on week. At present, there is quite a handful of requirements firmed up this week which did help ease some rate pressure.  We do, however, not anticipate much changes to the current rate levels seen. Moreover, there is limited improvement in the LNG prices, which kept the West-to-East arbitrage opportunities low. The continued lack of cross basin trades/arbitrage has also reduced ton-miles significantly, which in turn, would create relatively lengthy short-term supply of shipping in both basins as vessels fixed for a single voyage would quickly become available again. Some charterers were also seen using this opportunity now to inquire for multi month charters. Should the rates be fairly competitive, we do envisage Charterers securing vessel(s) for a longer duration, possibily into Q1 next year. This could very well prove to be a win-win for both parties, especially for Owners who value and target to achieve maximum vessel utilization.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The tone of the market hasn’t changed this week and a muted IP week attendance in London sums up the LNGC market. Headline rates continue their decline in tandem with ballast bonus sentiment, although market activity remains strong with numerous vessels coming into the week on subs and look set to go clean this week. The problem is more vessels keep turning up in all four corners of the globe at a rate above the number of vessels re-entering employment. Some charterers are looking to make the most of the situation with some conversations being protracted as charterers turn the screw in an effort to secure even lower econs. Cargo demand remains weak along with relatively low margins, and this is fueling a further squeeze on owners more than normal both for spot and multi-month charters.  New build activity remains quiet whilst live tenders continue to assess offers and prices remain stable.  In short, it will take a few months and potentially longer to rebuild the sentiment and clear the tonnage currently sitting on the water with prompt availability. We watch with interest.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Shipping rates are continuing their descending trend in both basins - quicker than one would expect, as lacklustre demand goes on. Cargo prices remain under pressure, offering minimal trading margins. In the West, increasing availability sees Independent Owners and Portfolio Players with excess length “fighting” for requirements. In such a market, utilisation for Owners is key, hence recent tests on levels have shown further drops. In the East, halt in demand and delays in Chinese ports on the back of the Corona virus see more diversions as well as floating storage situations, the levels of which, however, are not high enough to the extent we could see some recovery in rates. Nevertheless, should floating storage continue, we should not disregard the case of few extra requirements to emerge in this basin. Term tender activity is still active, but there were no NB orders recorded this week on conventional tonnage. In the midsize segment, PETRONAS signed a 12-year time charter party for two 79,960m3 newbuilding LNG vessels with “K”Line, on the back of orders at Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding (Group) Co. Ltd. The twin sister vessels, dubbed the “Wuhaogou-Max” or “W-Max” are specifically constructed to be fully optimised for the delivery of LNG supply commitments to Shenergy’s Wuhaogou LNG terminal in Shanghai, China.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The downward trends seen in recent weeks have continued, and by some measures have even accelerated in the LNG markets. Turning first to the cargo market, two of the major importing regions have seen large price falls, with JKM and TTF down ~20% and ~12%, respectively, week-on-week; set against a far more modest decline in HH pricing, trading margin are squeezed further. Uncertainty continues in the Far East, with cargoes delayed into or diverted away from China; the capacity for other importers to absorb the excess is being tested and the full impact of Force Majeure is yet to be seen. In response, the shipping market continues to cool. The competition for charters and in particular for utilisation is pushing rates lower. The lower cargo pricing is also narrowing the ST/TFDE/MEGI-XDF spread. It is not easy remaining optimistic in the current market, but with the latest reports showing coronavirus infection rates being in decline and if production remains strong, we could see interest in floating storage short term and a bounce in vessel demand and cargo pricing in the medium term.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Crazy times in the US markets with the FOB netbacks in great flux. In early Jan FOBs were netting back to multi year highs with deals being done in the low 30 cent per gallon range. At the beginning of this week, with fear gripping the markets over the coronavirus,  values had dropped all the way back to mid-single digits and there was even talk of cargo cancelations. Today the market seems to have settled around the 8 -10 cpg range for FOB cargos,  although fear and caution are still in charge.  Weekly Propane inventories increased by 600,000 barrels and are at nationwide levels normally formerly only seen during the summer months. Going forward we expect slow going until more certainty over China becomes clear.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: ASIA The big question this week is how the Coronavirus will effect the Chinese markets. Will an economic slowdown  reduce the Petchem cracking, PDH runs,  thus crashing demand or will the reduction of crude runs reduce the domestic LPG production and thus increase imports. We have seen an LNG cargo force majeured this week and there is serious concern this may happen with LPG cargos. If the Chinese markets are unable/unwilling to import LPG from the Middle East and the US, the outcome will be dire.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The past week has been subdued for LNGCs as they follow the wider energy markets, coming under more scrutiny than normal. The LNG cargo market has fallen close to record lows, with weak sentiment being reinforced by the extended public holidays in China and the impact on demand, with uncertainty ongoing. In the west, a prompt Atlantic requirement that kept bearish sentiment at bay last week has vanished. The region remains untested and although rates are reassessed lower, Atlantic availability looks ominous and we could see further falls. The East is currently in the midst of a competitive spot tender and whilst we await the results the amount of interest generated among "owners" again adds some downwards pressure to rates.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As we are nearing the end of January, shipping rates have seen further decline with more vessels expected to hit the market once redelivered by her present Charterers. Although the Atlantic market did provide some support with a handful of potential requirements and FOB cargo tenders seen loading from W. Africa and the US Gulf, the extended holidays, limited requirements in the East and an over supplied product market have put pressure on the current spot rates. It’s no surprise given that the shouldering months are resurfacing around this time of the year and as such, utilization is key. With that in mind, it seems tonnage providers are looking for multi month charter opportunities while most Charterers seem to prefer to only cover with spot charters instead.  Although there are no new building deals concluded this week, there are a handful of larger ongoing long-term tenders which could in turn see more delivery slots being reserved or firmed up from the shipyards.  After passing her 40th year birthday, another LNG vessel was sold for demolition last week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: EAST: Saudi posted February CP at respectively 505 $ and 545 $ for propane and butane, a 60 $ and 45 $ decrease respectively compared to January. Propane is higher than the market’s expectation, however, market has been at a halt with Chinese New Year break and we do not expect much activity east with present virus hitting China.  Players are waiting for march nominations acceptances with QP coming in the next days. Market is in strong backwardation with Feb/March CP at 20 $ with FEI at 12 $.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Confusion reigns. Crashing arb and terminalling fees has participants scratching their heads wondering if it really is January or have we actually morphed into a summer month. Netbacks for US Gulf cargos have come off close to 75 percent since their peak in just over 3 weeks leaving buyers and sellers worlds apart. Adding to the confusion is a CP price which seems way over valued and leaving US terminal operators wishing they could sell CP related. US inventories came off 3.7 million barrels for the week and this allowed propane prices to edge back over the thirty percent of WTI  value. Their were fog delays last week but exports showed up at a record 1.569 million barrels per day. We realize this takes into consideration pipeline , rail and truck exports as well as waterborne exports but we cant help but feel this level is a bit overdone.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The seasonal improvements in terms and market sentiment in the “Winter period” is now easing, with headline rates tapering off as vessel availability grows. The charter market faces backwardation in the coming weeks, and shipowners are looking to secure charters ahead of the shoulder months of March, April and May. The past week saw a handful of spot fixtures in both basins, mainly addressing a firm need of vessels due to fleet scheduling constraints rather than potential charters arising from trading opportunities; cargo optimization is creating more FOB sales but these are being picked up by players with their own shipping, leading to less chartering activity. Likewise, several opportunities that were initially for shipping instead resulted in FOB sales with no incremental spot shipping demand. This trend may continue as a significant number of the vessels available in the market for the next two months are sublets from projects, traders and portfolio players rather than those owned by independent shipowners, and the requirements that do lead to firm charters will be keenly fought over.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: ASIA: Happy Chinese New Year! One of the big questions overhanging the Asian market this week is when tariffs on LPG cargos into China will be lifted. This has put immense pressure on the CP price causing the derivative price for Feb CP to fall over USD 100/mt as well as causing the FEI price to fall as well. Is the lifting of tariffs bullish or bearish for the market. Certainly today the market is saying bearish. However if this opens the door to new projects in China the long term effects could actually turn out to be bullish.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Even prior to the EIA’s bullish propane stats, the Feb/March Arb narrowed considerably after large drops in the Asian paper market. While the netbacks weakened, a strong physical premium remains in the east, keeping US  FOB interest afloat and well above cancellation economics.  Levels are being discussed in the low 20cpg’s for the remaining February Houston-origin cargoes. However, shipping delays and unpredictably in the channel have caused for headwinds in some discussion. The EIA’s report, released Thursday due to the holiday weekend, showed a 1.4 million barrel draw in propane inventories. Inventories are now total 87 million barrels which is 27 percent above the 5 year average. The high inventory and lack of winter weather is keeping propane below 30 percent of WTI.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Swap price still stumbles this week. At the time of writing, Feb Propane CP weakened to $510 while Mar at deep backwardation at $452. However, butane CP has edged up due to tight MEG supply amid robust demand from India and Indonesia, currently traded at $550. Qatar Petroleum was reported to award their propane sale tender for 24/27th Feb lifting but the price is yet to know.  A bundle of Q2 lifting FOBs for equal ratio split were changing hand at loading month CP plus mid-single digit.   FAR EAST:  Far East market is strengthened due to the delay caused by foggy weather in US. Feb FEI/CP kept narrowing down from previous minus $20ish to minus $10. Bids on propane for 2h Feb were at Feb FEI plus mid-high 20s in window, while offers off window pegged at high 30s to $40.  Several Chinese PDH users are reported to have secured propane feedstock delivered in 2h Feb at the premium ranging from low-mid 80s to $90ish on Feb CP link, which equates to $20ish premium on FOB netback. Feb purchase has almost finished, and players started exploring on Mar arrival tons. Importers specialized in residential markets are quieter relatively, as domestic prices weakening with refinery destocking before CNY.   FPCC cancelled their buy tender for 22kt propane or 22/22 during end Feb delivery, and is expected to come out for Mar for better economy as widen spread between FEI and MOPJ in Mar than in Feb.   Indonesia PERTAMINA has issued tender to secure three equal ratio cargos delivered from end Feb to 1h Mar.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Mt Belvieu propane has come back below 30%  of WTI which is where we expect it to stay. After a 947,000 barrel draw US inventories standing at 87.9 million barrels for the week ending January 10th 2020. The inventory draw or build seems to be dictated by the amount of exports / day as opposed to the domestic demand and production which are holding fairly steady. This is a healthy level, 30% higher than the same week last year. Export capacity increases were seen as the big threat to having enough barrels in stock to survive the winter but production seems to have calmed this threat. With East and West arbs wide open, we expect freight to remain strong and terminalling fees as well. Finally the biggest news of the week seems to be the lifting of LPG tariffs in China on US LPG which is now scheduled to take place in April.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As we hit mid-January, we are starting to see more action in the spot market; however, this increase in enquiries is counterbalanced by more ships redelivering into the market, widening availability in both basins. The Pacific leads the way in activity, but prompt owners are swallowing this up quickly and rates are edging lower. The fixing window is now well into February, and although prompt vessels continue to gather in the basin we’ve not seen many Owners lured west for the prospect of better numbers in the Atlantic, perhaps because the lower availability is currently matched by fewer requirements. Portfolio players remain in charge of the tonnage situation in the basin, holding it stable and leaving room for optimization should they have the space to do so. With the Lunar New Year festivities starting at the back end of next week we could see a flux of demand pop up as market players hoping for some rest over the period look to cover themselves before the holidays begin. Yard prices remain unchanged since last week, and no new orders have been reported in the market.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Swap price is riding a roller coaster, as new year starts with uncertainties between Iran and US.  Earlier this week, Feb CP spiked up to $565 but rapidly plunged to $505 on Thurs, following the crude.  Qatar Petroleum has released Feb acceptances with delays reported from 5 to 12 days. Since most lifters nominated for early Feb laycan to avoid heavy backwardations, which assessed at $50 at the time of writing. QP has tendered to sell a 24/27th Feb lifting full propane cargo, which due at 14th Jan.  Other than this, limited FOB offers were seen, as lifters concerning acceptances for Adnoc and Saudi. The FEB FOB value ranges from small discounts to teens premium, subject to the loading laycan and ratio.   FAR EAST:  A handful of propane delivered in Feb into Japan/Korea are concluded this week. Premium starts higher early this week, with deals traded at Feb FEI plus 53$ for 1H Feb and $45 for 2h Feb, later declined to $40 mid-week. Despite the softening premium, Far East market still appears strong with MB/FEI arb opens wide, which props up the discussions on terminal fee premium for US fob liftings.  Moreover, continued tightness in Non-Us origin supply has buoyed up market sentiments. Several Chinese PDHs have carried out or going to have maintenance, partly due to negative margins and partly in lack of feedstocks. Offers for equal ratio cargos during 2h Feb delivery into China were heard at Feb CP plus 90s, whilst propane offers barely seen.  Indian HPCL has a term inquiry for 6 plus 3 optional equal ratio cargoes for 2020, which is reportedly still under negotiation. BPCL has issued buy tender to secure 800kt 50/50 ratio cargos from Mar 2020 to 2021, close by 20th Jan.   Indonesia PERTAMINA issued buy tender to secure two equal ratio cargos delivered in mid FEB several times, with nothing being awarded reportedly.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Mt Belvieu propane prices remain at 30% of WTI. This is due to global uncertainty caused to the US-Iran situation. Which meant the unexpected build of 690 000 barrel in propane inventories did not have the bearish affect on Mt Belvieu prices you would usually expect to see. US inventories are now at 88.9 million, 29% above this week last year and 17% higher than the 5 year average. We have seen Mt Belvieu Non-LST January propane discounted by 2cpg to LST January propane. This disparity has been attributed to very high production, and export capacity constraints leading to a glut of product in the caverns. The stratospheric rise US terminalling fees over the past few months, with recent January and February FOB slots being sold above 30cpg, is showing signs of slowing down for the first time. The US-FEI arb has narrowed and this coupled with rising freight rates form the region has eroded netback values.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It seems that the 2020 business year effectively only started this week as the majority of the market players returned to their desks from their holidays. There has been more activity in all of the basins this week, with a number of fresh spot requirements emerging together with one long-term shipping tender from a European utility. However, due to the lack of fixtures in the recent weeks, the spot rates continue to stay under pressure as the number of available tonnage have increased. Yet, if we continue to see further requirements developing, especially ahead of the impending Chinese New Year, we might see rates holding better than expected as the overall shipping length is not that drastic. Furthermore, the increasing unrest in the Middle-East is causing some concern to those who have LNG cargoes in and out from the region, and the potential ramifications to the shipping market still remains unknown. IMO2020 regulations are also now in full-force and we are already seeing the spread between low-sulphur fuel and high-sulphur fuel rise to highest levels seen in years, as quoted prices for low-sulphur fuels have soared. Albeit LNG shipping is less affected by the surge of low-sulphur fuel prices, this will definitely have an impact on ballast bonus discussions and Owners' decision on heel retention after voyages. On the newbuilding front, there were no new orders this week, although it was post reported that Hyundai Samho Heavy industries got the final LNGC newbuilding order for the calendar year 2019.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Firstly, Happy New Year! We wish everyone a prosperous 2020.   The week leading up to New Year has been quiet as LNG chartering experts (who planned ahead) took a well deserved break, the consequence has been limited vessel requirements West of Suez and the same can also be said for East of Suez.  Availability remains tight in the West with portfolio players running the show on prompt vessel tonnage, which will result in levels remaining stable. On the contrary, in the East there seems to be some added availability which is a cause for concern for ship owners.    Looking back, we can certainly say that 2019 was a year with seasonal rate fluctuations, reaching an unexpected low during Q2, to then firm up through Q3 and Q4. LNG prices were however «flattish» with limited to non existent West to East arbitrage in the main, but did see a mini-armada set sail in September for discharges in November.  LNG trading pattern - we saw more intra-basin activity as LNG stayed «local». 2019 was also a busy year for the few remaining LNG building Yards, as new orders remained robust throughout the year with a total count of 42 orders. What 2020 will bring is yet to be seen...but we at Fearnleys see another year with strong volume growth, more focus on «greener» shipping and some interesting trends worth monitoring. Hence, we are looking forward to the new opportunities of this New Decade! Once again we wishing you a Prosperous and Happy New Year!

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: In the Atlantic, weather has caused some disruption in South Hook and strikes have created delays in France. These have started to ease, particularly in South Hook. So as Father Christmas loads his sleigh, LNG parcels are arriving thick and fast. The arbitrage has widened as the West sees a softening at a quicker pace than in the East. A cargo tender in the Middle East has kept players working this week whilst tight availability in the West sees many checking in to assess potential needs. Turning to the availability, the market remains balanced yet with the signs of additional length starting to appear in the East. With no profitable inter-basin arbitrage and limited independent Owners in the Atlantic, levels are likely to hold despite the lack of a flurry of obvious long-haul routes. Why? Portfolio tonnage makes up the majority of the availability and while these vessels flirt with the ideas of subletting they can quickly retreat to the portfolio for internal business leaving one or two players to negotiate it out.   The New build market saw a lot of activity as the contracts for the Shell NB program firmed up this week, resulting in more orders and leaving the number of available vessels untouched. Will we run out of yard space? unlikely at this moment in time and prices remain flat. Just leaves us just to say - we wish everyone a very pleasant break during this festive period and we will leave the sentimental commentary for next week as we look back on 2019 but more importantly forward to 2020.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: For a week that saw relatively few fixtures and broadly static rates, there sure were enough intriguing developments to keep everyone on their toes. The Atlantic saw a combination of factors disrupt trade flows, including continuing long queues for cargoes into the UK, severe storms in the Bay of Biscay and industrial action in France impacting some discharges. The additional time on water for laden cargoes and slower ballast passages raised concerns among charterers with tight schedules, and with issues continuing through the week coupled with the first exports out of Freeport we may see an uptick in fixing levels. The Pacific hasn't seen the same excitement, but continues to tick over with a steady flow of requirements for owners to work. It hasn't all been rosy for owners though, as charterers can take comfort in the amount of interest generated by a multi month requirement from the spring. As we approach the final week before Christmas and the last fortnight of the year, we hope both owners and charterers can find some festive cheer.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco’s Jan lifting acceptance has astonished the whole market, with cancellations/delays/cuts/grade changes happening. This being said, the front supply has tightened up further.  Due to this, swap value has shot up again this week. At the time of writing, Jan propane CP is traded at $507, $67 higher than Jan CP, and butane rose up to $531 with continuous $25 gap. Feb CP chased up, traded at $487 with $20 backwardation, and we believe the spread might narrow down further as Feb supply doesn’t look abundant either.  Qatar Petroleum was reported to award their sell tender for 27/29th lifting full C3 to one Chinese importer at CP plus high single premium.   FAR EAST: Very eventful market this week before Christmas, with various bids in/off window on either US/non-US and tenders floating.  Propane for 2h Jan delivery is bid at Jan FEI plus mid 30s or flat price $564 while no seller seen. Mid-Jan lifting equal ratio cargos is being bid at $515/545 but again nothing concluded.   Equal ratio demand appears strong with SEA inquiries. One Vietnam importer has issued buy tender to secure two parcels of equal ratio cargos delivered in 21st Dec till 1h Jan and 25th Jan to 10th Feb, and the result is yet to know. Meanwhile, Indonesia Pertamina has issued new tender to secure two evenly split cargo as well, but delivered during early and mid Feb, which valid till tomorrow.   However, demand into China is still mainly driven by propane for petchem use. One SChina Importer has bought 2h Jan arrival 23/0 at mid-80s, luckily we would say, since apart from this, still several rigid demand haven’t been covered. Despite the squeezed margins on PDHs, some plants with downstream complex still have profits and keep exploring cargos. However, several failed to award their buy tenders for propane delivered from 2h Jan till 1h Feb as in lack of offers. Some readjust the program and try deferring into Feb purchase, otherwise might need to lower down run rate before running out of feedstock.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: A larger than expected 2.5 million barrel draw in Mt Belvieu did nothing to change the slide in Mt Belvieu values vs WTI. Mt Belvieu now lies below 35% WTI and inventories remain high at 91 million barrels, which has been keeping downward pressure on Mt Belvieu propane prices. With demand ramping up in the East the arb is wide open, and some recent softness in the freight market has led to very high netback values. Due to this we have seen the 4 week average of exports climb to 1.3 million barrels of propane per day. This trend looks set to continue as FOB buying interest from the US is very strong and every ton which can be, is being exported. The question now is will recently set FOB values of 20cpg become the new normal or will FOB values continue to increase? In South America, news of the winner of the 1.3 million ton Petro Ecuador tender is keenly being awaited.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: We are only in the second week of December but with the reduced activity it feels as though the holiday mood may have already hit the market. As overall availability has increased slightly, spot rates continue to soften from recent highs although so far both headline levels and voyage economics remain broadly positive. Therefore, the delicate market balance continues to hold, and could yet tilt further towards charterers or swing back in owners’ favour,  especially if the build-up of vessels waiting to discharge at certain terminals leads to prolonged floating storage. There is more action on the long term side, with continuing newbuild tenders for charterers looking to secure slots prior to the anticipated ordering boom for Qatari and Mozambique volume, among others.    Maran has contracted two new MEGI 174k CBM vessels at DSME for delivery in 2022.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Price shoots up this week amid robust demand. Jan CP has traded at $475, up by $30 WoW and butane is traded at $25 higher.  ADNOC has announced their Jan lifting with 7-10 days delays reportedly, and some ratio being changed from equal ratio to heavy propane.  Qatar Petroleum has issued a sale tender for a full propane loading 29/31th Jan, which ratio is very attractive to Chinese Petchem buyers.   FOB discussions are active with India and Indonesia buy tenders flowing in the market. One late Jan lifting equal ratio cargo was reported traded at Jan CP minus small discount, as Jan/Feb CP falls into over $25 backwardation. Whilst other earlier liftings, which can make within Jan arrival, are assessed at the value of at least $5-10 premium.    FAR EAST: Very heated market with bullish sentiment for whatever origins.  23kt propane for 2h Jan delivery have been traded from Jan FEI plus $13 Monday, to plus $29 on Thursday, which equates to Jan CP plus around $55. And off window still many buyers exploring 2h Jan arrival tons. Non-Us origin cargoes also in strong demand from not only SEA, but also China.  India IOC has issued tender to buy two equal ratio cargoes delivered in Jan and Indonesia Pertamina has also tender to buy 29/31th Jan 22/22 CFR into Kalbut.  Chinese importers are bidding aggressively for Jan and even Feb arrival propane. Earlier this week one Chinese importer managed to secure 23kt propane for 1h Jan arrival at Jan CP plus high 60s. Another SChina Petchem buyer has just closed tender to buy 23kt propane for 16-25th Jan delivery, which still in validity. Players assessed the cash premium will easily exceed $70 as front market too tight, against too many propane inquires from petchem rigid demand. One Chinese player is reported that awarded on the latest Sonangol tender for 7/9th Jan lifting heavy propane and has placed the propane parcel into EChina.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The Mt Belvieu propane price fell to 37% WTI after bearish inventories. A surprise build of 1.7 million barrels was seen when market expectations were for a draw of 2 million barrels for the week ended December 6th. This is very much a sellers’ market for US FOBs with many vessels available to lift and buyers queuing up to buy any tons which become available. These market factors have led to another week of extremely high exports of 1.538 million barrels per day. We expect these record high export figures to continue as wide arbs, and freight rates from the US under pressure, means traders are trying to squeeze every possible ton out for export. The last week has been warmer in the US and domestic demand has come off by around 1 million barrels per day. Once winter rears it’s head in the US the questions is how large will the weekly draws be and how quickly will Mt Belvieu react narrowing the arb?

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Winter market is here and Arb is popping. As stated before the NWE and Eastern markets have come to rely on the US as the principal supplier and as a result the Arb is, and will remain firmly open for the foreseeable future. It is even seems to have evolved in to what economist like to call a Goldy Locks scenario,  where it is neither too hot nor too cold,  but just right. With today’s economics , terminal operators are making money, ship owners are making money,  and traders seem happier than they have for a few years. These markets never seem to last but for now it is hard to see how and when it will end. In the domestic market propane inventories drew 1.7 million barrels on the week which was in line with industry expectations. There is enough propane in the US to support cold weather and strong exports and hence we do not expect prices to blow out either way.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Qatar Petroleum has released Jan lifting schedule with a few delays being reported, mainly due to early-month nominations.  Swap price has ridden a roller coaster this week, with Jan CP being traded from $431 in mid-week to $444 at the time of writing.  End Dec lifting FOB was traded at small premium on Jan CP, and sellers with Jan lifting Fobs also targeted at premium level, especially seeing robust demand into Asia in front amid softening freight.   FAR EAST:  1H Jan CFR Asia Market appear tight, either US or Non-Us origin.  Off window 23kt US-origin propane for 1h Jan delivery is traded at Jan FEI plus $13-14. Discussion for similar cargo delivered in 2h Jan is slightly cheaper but sellers’ ideas hover above teens on FEI link as well.  Non-US origin supply for 1h Jan arrival is short as well. One SChina PDH user has secured 23kt propane for 1h Jan delivery at Jan CP plus mid 60s via tender, while another Major also purchased a full propane for mid/2h Jan delivery at Jan CP plus 60ish.   However not every buyer is that lucky to cover their demand. Till the time of writing, Indonesia Pertamina was reported not covering the 22/22 demand for 1-6th Jan delivery; One Echina petchem user was said that not cover their prompt demand for 23kt propane delivered from 2h Dec into 1h Jan; even Taiwan CPC tender for 11/11 delivered during 1-10th Jan was not heard awarded either. Some Chinese importers has reprogramed and tried to defer their demand into 2h Jan arrival. Apart from spot inquiries, term discussion are still going on. Mid-week one Schina importer was said to cancel their term inquires for 11/11 monthly as the received offers not satisfactory.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
