x: We are in the last month of the final quarter of 2019 and what was predicted to be a robust Q4 2019 has not exceeded Owners’ expectations. Ship Owners enjoyed a mini-boom from early October, however the firm sentiment was short-lived as the market has moderated in the last few weeks. The lacklustre performance of the product market, subdued shipping demand for the winter and an increase in tonnage availability, not just from Independent Owners but also sublets, have contributed to the sentiment change.  The Atlantic Basin kept some balance with prompt cargoes and limited availability, but Owners with ships in the Pacific may feel the pinch as we see rates slip below six- to high five-digit levels due to the lack of activity and cargo demand in the region. However, it’s not all gloomy as fixing levels are still healthy and for most Owners, “in the money”. The concern is more for the post winter season next year where many, including us, anticipate a slightly more challenging environment.  Utilization is key for those months and could mean more inclination from Owners to work competitive rates now for longer duration to brace the shouldering period. That said, rate ideas would need to connect.  For the longer term charters, the future looks active for Owners as a good handful of Oil Majors, Trading Houses and Projects were seen issuing tender documents to secure vessels for delivery between 2022-2025.  On the newbuilding front, Samsung announced 8 orders - believed to be linked to Mozambique LNG - and more orders from them are expected.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It has been another relatively quiet week, which is slightly surprising considering we are close to the peak winter period historically speaking. On the cargo side, we are seeing a handful of supply tenders, but it seems that these are not creating a massive interest in the market, again highlighting the looming global oversupply of LNG. However, it might as well be that with the current low-price LNG environment, fewer players are willing to take an extra cargo on their books for a small risk/reward ratio so late in the fiscal year and rather focus on how to decorate their Christmas tree this winter. The few shipping requirements that has been worked this week have proved that there is indeed downward pressure on the rates in both basins, albeit the situation in the Pacific looks more challenging for the owners than in the Atlantic, where the vessel availability is still very tight. That said, by all means it is not all doom and gloom for the rest of the year, since we are yet to see how the winter weather will develop, and as we have witnessed before, things can change in a heartbeat in the world of LNG. From the newbuilding side, Samsung Heavy Industries secured an LNG carrier order worth of USD 1.5 billion for a yet undisclosed Eurasian shipowner for delivery by Q3 2022.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco has set Dec Propane CP at $440 and Butane CP at $455, up by $10 respectively, which some players reckon above expectations. Therefore, the contango structure into Jan has changed and Jan CP slides to $438. It’s still early to judge how will Jan CP turns, but we believe the Jan swap will edge up, as forthcoming winter demand will lend support fundamentally.    FAR EAST:  Front market appears to be strong this week. Off window Propane for 2h Jan delivery was reported traded at Jan FEI plus high single prem to $10. Dec FEI/CP enlarged to 50ish this week and Jan FEI/CP maintains at high 30s to $40. The unexpected explosion in Texas has roused some concerns on Jan delivery so far limited effect being shown, but players are still closely monitoring the situation.  Apart from window, market is floating with all tenders. Indonesia Pertamina was reported to award their last tender for three evenly split cargos delivered from early Jan to late Jan, price ranging from high 40s to high 50s depends on delivery date. And they’ve still inquiring via new tender for another early Jan delivery cargo, which result is yet to know.  India IOC is reported to award their buy tender for 2h Jan delivery equal ratio cargo at Jan CP plus 50ish.  Taiwan FPCC also secured an early Jan delivery full propane at Jan MOPJ minus around $40 via tender. Other Chinese importers are actively seeking supply for next year via term tender or private discussions. Cash premium negotiation is in line with freight as of non-Us origin request, but more players are keen to discussing FEI link as well, instead of 100% CP link. On spot side, importers start to explore Jan cargos especially 1h Jan arrival, with one SChina PDH user tendered to buy 6-15th Jan delivery propane.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Happy Thanksgiving! A lower than expected draw of 683,000 barrels was seen in US inventories for the week ended November 22nd. Although this was expected to be bearish, Mt Belvieu now lies at 41% WTI. The highest level since March of this year. This has not dampened the arb which is wide. Supported by strength in both CIF ARA and FEI. The affects of the fire at Port Neches on LPG exports from Nederland are yet to be seen. Nederland exports range between 6 and 8 VLGCs per month and for the moment the Neches river channel is closed. Any export tons lost would further support the arb. January cargoes have traded and high single digit terminalling fees. The question is was it a pre holiday rush, or are we heading back to double digit terminalling fee premiums?

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Sentiment softened throughout the week as a lack of requirement was felt in both basins. Despite the lack of activity, the ideas being discussed suggest that expectations are being lowered in terms of what rates can be achieved.  More tonnage became available both prompt and into the New Year in the Pacific and while the Atlantic and Middle East remain tight, there’s still not enough requirement in the market to add much positivity to the rates. Unsold volume still lingers in both Basins, and with muted demand, it seems to push product prices down. That combined with an increase in tonnage availability, have reduced the Bullish sentiment the market held not too long ago. One continuing uncertainty that may support tonnage providers is the prospect of floating storage – we’ve seen more floaters discharging recently but with inventories remaining high we might not have seen the end of floating storage. That said, with the declining sentiment we’re currently being exposed to, the risk is that we may see rates softening as the fixing window moves closer and closer to the New Year, unless we see a sudden surge in requirements. Term tender activity is high, but no large LNG newbuilding orders were reported this week and prices remain stable.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Some bitterly cold weather in the US and  late season crop drying led to a higher than expected 3.4 million barrel draw in US inventories. This, as expected, was bullish Mt Belvieu prices which now stand at 40% WTI. Rather than closing the arb this rise in Mt Belvieu dragged FEI and CIF ARA prices up with it maintaining a healthy level. This has kept January FOB discussion active and being worked well in advance of the Christmas break. US inventories are 12.43 million barrels higher than the same week last year. Exports for the week were 1.362 million barrels per day, remain very high which points our view that the world has grown to depend on US exports and we expect this to continue at least through the Winter.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Another volatile week with flat price rolling up and down by $15 on daily basis. At the time of writing, Dec CP is traded at $417, while butane at $15 higher. Forward month is in backwardation as Dec/Jan CP maintains at $5/6. Despite such, Jan market is expected to improve as real winter demand kicks in.  Fob discussions for 1h Dec are still at discounted level, with last mid Dec FOB sale from KPC reporting at Dec CP minus mid-single digit. One Producer is said to have spot availability in 1h Dec lifting.    FAR EAST: Window is not very exciting with sellers asking Dec FEI plus $8 for 2h Dec 23/0, while off window deal level for similar cargo at plus $3-3.5 only. Most players have balanced their Dec position and Japan/Korean importers are not keen on speculative buying considering year-end stock.    Off window market is quite active with tenders flowing and Chinese covering shorts especially for petchem use. Indonesia Pertamina was reported awarded one equal ratio cargo for 1h Jan delivery at Dec CP plus 50s, and following this, they’ve reissued new buy tender to purchase four evenly-split cargos delivered from early to 2h Jan. However, other evenly-split cargo for 2h Dec delivery into SEA is reported done at Dec CP plus high 40s only, as no more buyers can take such early laycan.   Spot deals into China this week is more propane heavy related. Last Friday one heavy propane was sold into SChina at Dec CP plus high 50s. And this week, a couple of pure propane were sold at Dec CP plus 60s to around $70, depending on delivery destination, for petchem use. Other than spot, one SChina importer has issued term tender to secure 11/11 monthly, either 1st decade delivery from Jan to Dec, or 2nd to 3rd decade delivery from Mar to Dec.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The intensity of the October market seems to have eased off as we arrive here in mid-November. New vessel availabilities have been observed, rather on regular basis in the East. Outright availability of LNG vessels in the West are still few and far between, but FOB/DES swaps seems to solve it for now. In the Pacific, there seem to be more LNG vessels available than there are spot chartering opportunities, for the moment.   We are now perceived to have come “back to normal” since the elimination of the US/China sanctions effects. However, many are of the opinion that current levels are where the market should be if the recent sanctions did not happen. This have led to speculation of a possible “double peak” as the anticipated winter activity has not gone full blown as yet, but this view have been disputed with the claim of soft demand for LNG imports in China for these upcoming months. For certain, the LNG shipping market have been more volatile recently as weather and geo-political movements or announcements could lead to tremendous shift in sentiments.   No newbuilding orders or ship sales have been reported this week. However, a few ships are being circulated in the SnP market.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Cold weather coupled with strong crop drying demand has pushed up domestic propane demand, and as result weekly inventories drew 2. 5 million barrels. A rise in motor gasoline and the blending of butane into gasoline has pushed up domestic butane demand. These factors combined with strong exports have allowed domestic prices to increase substantially over the last month. Now the question is will these price increases  close the arb or will international prices keep pace. If we were asking this question in March , we might say no,  but in November our answer is we expect International prices to keep pace.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Swap market value edged up this week. Dec Propane rebounded to $415, and Dec FEI/CP spread has further enlarged from mid 30s last week to mid/high 40s. With acceptance for Dec lifting being released, players starting to engage actively in FOB discussion, but bids are at discount level as of soaring freight.   KPC issued a sale tender to offer a 14/15 Dec lifting 22/22, the result is yet to know at the time of writing.   Qatar Petroleum has officially announced a ten-year agreement with Wanhua Chemical to supply roughly 800,000 tons LPG annually. Just in last Nov, Wanhua also signed a ten-year purchase agreement to ADNOC to secure 1 million tonne LPG per year.   FAR EAST:  Front window is strengthening this week. During mid-week, 23kt Propane for 2h Dec delivery is traded at Dec FEI plus $6. As Dec FEI/CP keep widening, the US/Non-Us origin spread has rapidly narrowing down. We might soon see players deliver non Us origin into Japan/Korea range instead of swarming into China.   Spot inquiries from China remains slim, compare to recent term discussion. One EChina PDH issued a mini term tender to secure 23/0 or 46/0 in Jan and Feb but later withdrew as offers not attractive. One 11/11 for 1h delivery into Schina was reported done at Dec CP plus around $60 only.   Indonesia Pertamina was reported to awarded their tender for a equal ratio split cargo delivered mid Dec at Dec CP plus high 40s, which is roughly Dec CP flattish or small discount on FOB netback.   CPC was reported awarded their buy tender at Dec CP plus low mid 60s for the purchase of one 11/11 delivered in 2h Dec. And they’ve issued a FOB/DES term tender to swap a volume of 176k-264k AG FOB cargos for 176k cargos Des into Taiwan. Considering 20 Cal freight level, there might be limited parties can commit such.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: LNG rate market phrenic seems to be slowly easing, as the effect of US/China sanctions eliminates, however there are still a couple of upcoming requirements that need coverage especially in the East. Charterers looking at securing a vessel today for late November or December loadings, still have to pay six-digit figures as prompt availability remains tight. Looking at the spot availability going forward it is expected that a few vessels that caught the Oct-Nov arbitrage will start redelivering. That might put pressure on rates. However, we might see some of those vessels looking at business West of Suez as West to East arbitrage is very slowly reviving. In the Atlantic, prompt availability has dried up, however a few opportunistic sublets appear here and there from portfolio players, as FOB cargo optimisations look like a preferred option for them creating some potential length, but with limited flexibility. Despite high tender activity, newbuilding prices remain stable for now....

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Despite the crude rise, the Dec CP plunged to $398 at the time of writing, whilst Dec FEI/CP spread fluctuates from $29 to $36. QP has released their Dec lifting nomination with some delays by 5 days or so being reported. Baltic continues to rise until mid-week stabilizes at $75ish. This being said, few fixtures happening in MEG and the soaring freight has erodes buyer’s appetite to explore FOB spot.   FAR EAST: This week front market is weakening. Propane for 1H Dec delivery was traded at Dec FEI plus $5 and dropped further to $3 reportedly. 2h Dec also traded in similar level earlier this week, with slight backwardation only. Some importers are closely monitoring year-end stock and avoiding over purchase.   Off window there are some traders’ inquires for prompt delivery into India and Indonesia which supports butane price a bit, despite the bids are in discounts on FOB netbacks. One reason being is less butane from US available as arbitrage window closed now, therefore players has turned to explore AG origin.   Other than such, last Fri one South China PDH user has awarded their buy tender for 23/0 1st decade delivery in Dec at Dec CP plus around $60, and they’ve issued another buy tender for similar cargo delivered in mid Dec. And one more propane cargo reported sold into North China at Nov CP plus around/below $70, which equates to CP minus mid-single digit discount. Other Chinese also exploring heavy propane cargos in 2h Dec delivery. CPC issued buy tender for 11/11 or 0/11 delivered in late Dec, result is yet to know.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: A surprise build of 300,000 barrels was seen in US inventories. The hope that this would be bearish for Mt Belvieu prices was short-lived. Mt Belvieu continued to increase through this build due to cold weather biting on the East Coast and in the Midwest. This strength in Mt Belvieu which now lies at 38% of WTI has been steadily eroding the arb. Help will need to come from price strength in demand markets. For now FOB trades have quietened down. This is due to the shift form double digit terminalling fee discussions for full propane FOB cargoes, down to just above cancellation levels, around 6cpg. Traditionally the onset of US winter is early than in Europe and the East. Now the question is when will it get cold in those demand markets?

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The lower than expected draw in US inventories of 100,000 bbls took the total inventories to 99.8 million barrels. The draw was bearish against expectations but Mt Belvieu went up. Last week the inventory number was bullish and Mt Belvieu went down. Go figure, but with that said the first real cold weather of the season has arrived and this domestic demand may be the real reason for the domestic price strength. This has coupled with rising freight rates has brought netback values down and traders FOB bid ideas down into single figures for December. We seemed to have reached a stalemate of sellers not willing to go below double figures FOB premiums and sellers not willing to pay up. Cargoes have been being worked a long way in advance to the usual 30-40 days prior laycan due to tight freight. The question is who will blink first for the few remaining FOB cargoes available this year? Buyers paying up or sellers coming down?

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco has set the November Propane CP at $430 and Butane CP at $445, each up by $10 from October price.  The Propane CP is in line with latest swap value, yet some end users/importers reckon it is higher than expectation. Also, the spread between Propane and Butane is wider than latest trade which was at $10.  At the time of writing, December CP is traded at $410, $20 less than the just announced November CP. December FEI/CP spread is traded at around $35, partly driven by the sustained strong freight.  Qatar Petroleum is reported to have awarded their December lifting of a full cargo Propane at December CP plus a small digit premium to a Chinese Major.   FAR EAST: A flurry of deals was concluded in the window this week. 23kt Propane for 2h November delivery was traded at November FEI plus $14, and one equal ratio cargo for end November delivery into Chiba was done at November CP plus $77, which equates to November CP plus $5 on FOB netback.  Off window discussions on Propane for December delivery are also active with a few trades concluded at December FEI plus mid-high single digit during mid-week. However, the levels currently under discussion are weakening.  One S.China PDH operator issued a buy tender to secure a 1-10 December delivery of 23/0, the result is yet to be known by the time of writing.  Other Chinese importers are cautious and want to think twice before taking spot cargoes in December before CP is set, importers also se sluggish demand from domestic customers combined with surplus supply from refineries.  Nevertheless, importers still expect strong rising demand and are starting inquire for next year’s term supplies but some discussions are still pending with uncertainties on US-China tariffs and strong freights in 2020.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Some cause for a pause in the chartering market as sanction news and its effects dissipate and chartering requirements pull back from the recent sprint.  This news couldn't come soon enough for some, yet a couple of prompt cargoes remain effected by its wake and those holding the cargoes continue to weigh up the choice between taking a ship at year highs or selling FOB at slightly better numbers. This challenging market has seen some creativity which is great to see. There aren’t too many Picasso’s out there and the LNG chain doesn’t provide a white canvas backdrop to go crazy but there are still some individuals/companies making grounds with ideas that should be common place. Creativity does face a challenging compromise, in a tight market the chartering equivalent to a silent assassin normally comes out on top but right now chartering departments are just one cog of a complex string of adjustments that takes time to align. This inability to move quickly carries its own risks. The result is lots of activity, questions and requirements and bigger differences between gains and losses.   The biggest movement in shipping economics this week is to the ballast bonus sentiment whilst further out one year and multi-year rates take a slide, thus rates relatively stable this week but overall economics are starting to drift downwards. New build prices are stable yet under pressure whilst second hand prices continue their downward trend.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: November CP has fluctuated thruout this week, amidst concerns over general supply and lukewarm demand. Despite the rise in crude and a FOB bid at $435 for a fixed date November lifting of full cargo Propane, November CP was traded at $410 only. November CP C3/C4 spread narrowed to $10 today, due to more Butane was loaded out of US and less than expected disruptions in supply ex MEG. Saudi Aramco’s November acceptances was reported with some delays but no  Although not usual during the winter season, November/December swaps show a $15 backwardation structure. Qatar Petroleum issued a sales tender to sell a full cargo Propane loading during 1st to 28th Dec, being a flexible loading window.  FAR EAST: In a strong Far East window with bids mainly seen. 23kt Propane for 2h Nov delivery was bid at November FEI plus $14, in fact 1 booking took place at FEI plus $13 or fixed price at $451. Off window similar cargo was traded at November FEI plus mid/high teens. This being said, US origin cargo value has risen, which in turn has squeezed the spread to non US origin tons, from previous over $50 to latest less than $30.  Indonesia’s Pertamina issued yet another new tender to purchase one evenly split cargo for delivery of 5-7th Dec into Kalbut. They reportedly awarded their last tender for similar cargo for early December delivery into Teluk Semangka at November CP plus  Demand for Non-US origin cargo slowed down this week, as most Chinese buyer having already covered their demand and incremental domestic supply into the residential market. In turn this lead to quite a dramatic change this week, with several Chinese importers heard reselling tons due to high inventory. Baltic took an initial nosedive by as much as $10 week before stabilizing , which depressed the cash premium for November arrival cargoes. Monday saw one S. China PDH buyer secure a 23/0 late November delivery at November CP plus low 60s only, following that an equal ratio cargo into S.China was concluded at plus 50ish.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: A draw of 460,000 barrels in US inventories has left stocks at 100 million barrels on the nose,  and despite this slightly larger than expected draw, global LPG markets have weakened. Mt Belvieu propane has come down to 34% of WTI, from 36% earlier in the week. Mt Belvieu butane also saw a large loss in value post inventories and now stands at 46% of WTI, down from 49% the previous day. Both drops seem a bit odd as propane’s comes on top of the first cold weather forecast and an inventory drop while butanes comes with a strengthening gasoline market.  There has been a noticeable drop in VLGC exports form PADD 1, Marcus Hook due to the majority of C4 being kept for domestic gasoline blending. US FOB stems available for trade through the end of the year are thin. The backwardation in CIF ARA and FEI markets is keeping interest for FOB cargoes prompt. We do not expect sellers to offer these remaining cargoes cheaply, so it will be interesting to see if the buyers or sellers win this battle.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The strong market continued this week as rates remained in the solid six-figures with three way economics, but there are signs that the sharp shock to the market may be easing. Much of the recent bullish sentiment was driven by a flurry of activity coupled with a very tight shipping market in the East; however, the easing of US/China sanctions and vessels redelivering into the spot market will likely reduce those pressures, and owners’ focus may now pass to the West. The West/East arbitrage, which has long been closed, is showing signs of life while tonnage in the Atlantic has all but dried up. There is potential for ballasting from the East and also the release of portfolio vessels, which have already been marketed albeit with restricted availability and a tendency to be withdrawn as internal requirements evolve. On several fronts then, the rollercoaster rides on. There were no new orders placed for newbuilds.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The 300,000 barrel draw in US inventories was slightly below expectations and is not expected to have a big effect on the Mt Belvieu price. US inventories remain above 100 million barrels, which is keeping the Mt Belvieu price well around 36% of WTI. With cooler than average temperatures on the way for much on the US we expect to see more draws in PADD 1 as product is moved from secondary to tertiary storages. These draws are unlikely to change the plentiful US supply picture with the 4 week average of production at 2.172 million barrels per day.  Most traders expect with over 100 million barrels in inventories and domestic production above 2 million barrels per day. There will be enough product to see winter through, including the additional export capacity built this year. For this reason the arb from the US is maintaining it’s strength as USGC FOB terminalling fee discussions are still in double figures.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Rates are firm, but stable from last week, except from some minor adjustments to reflect the most recent discussions. Prompt availability is tight, but at the same time, the high rates has lured some sub-letters to the surface. However, its proven difficult to match these positions with outstanding shipping requirements due to the sub-let vessels often restricted window of availability. Market is expected to remain tight over the coming weeks as multiple factors are impacting the balance in the shipping market.   We’ve had four newbuilds added to the orderbook by BW and MISC for delivery in 2022. BW may be speculative, MISC is basis term contracts with Exxon.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: The continuing high freight is killing buyer’s appetite to lift FOBs and we see AG lifters reoffering their FOBs instead of chartering in vessels.  One early November lifting 2/2 is being reported sold at November CP minus small digit to a China major who had shipping length available meeting the laycan. Saudi acceptances was finally announced and so far only minor delays being reported. November CP has been sliding most of this week $417 at the time of writing. Reasons for this include high freights and crude softening as well.    FAR EAST: Premium still edged up for Propane with delivery in November in the window. We have seen bids for 23kt Propane to bedelivered in 2h November climing up to high single digit based on November FEI while offers haven’t appeared yet. A couple of 2h November delivery for full Propane have been traded into Japan and Korea at flat to small premium levels. Players reckon that although ample supply from US at such wide arbitrage window, latest loading of equal ratio tons destined for South and South East Asia has alternatively restricted the full Propane liftings, given existing export capacities. Demand from South and SE Asia continue to be robust, with Indian and Indonesian tenders flowing in the market. BPCL issued buy tender for one equal ratio cargo for 1h November delivery, and Pertamina issued a buy tender to secure another two equal ratio cargoes for early Dec delivery.  At the same time, trades into China are also very active. Several PDH Buyers have secured Propane for November at the premium of over CP + $70 since late last week. One newly started PDH plant in S.China secured one full Propane cargo for 1H November delivery at November CP plus high $60s last week and issued another tender to purchase 23kt Propane for end Nov delivery.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The LNG shipping market has exceeded expectations this week. The lack of firm vessel availability and a rush of spot cargoes seen earlier have driven rates into the six digits, breaking through $100,000 for the first time since early January this year.  Sentiments are extremely bullish at the moment and Owners with vessels available for end October to November were carefully evaluating their options; it was clear to the market that the number of cargoes surpassed the ships available for charter. Furthermore, although most of the requirements seen are for intra-basin voyages, there were also a good mix of forward and fairly prompt cargoes. As such, the tables turned as Owners began requesting offers instead of offering their ships to Charterers, and as outlandish as it would have sounded a month back, ships were snapped up almost immediately at terms favorable to the Owners.  This evidently shows how illiquid the LNG shipping market is and how it can generate such high volatility when the supply or demand changes rapidly. With the amount of cargoes still left uncovered, we would expect rates to continue to soar this week.  On the newbuilding front, there are no new reports of transaction seen this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The smaller than expected 132,000 barrel build in US inventories strengthened Mt Belvieu prices. The draw in PADD 1 of 900,000 barrels suggest domestic retailers are readying for winter and stocking up before the cold weather hits. Whereas the build in PADD 3 of 1 million barrels for the week points to continued strong production and more butane exports. The PADD 3 stock level of 62.1 million barrels for the week ended October 4th is very large showing producers see Mt Belvieu as the best value for their tons. Mt Belvieu prices have strengthened to 39% of WTI. This  has not had an affect on exports with a strengthening global LPG market. Terminalling fees remains healthy as the arb continues to support strong freight levels. Cancellations are unthinkable in this market and traders are wondering if double digit FOB terminalling fees are here to stay..

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: After the quietness of last week, with it’s limited liquidity, November CP  saw a rapid rebound this week.  Compared to 1 week ago, November CP has gone up by $45 to $430 at the time of writing.  Baltic also risen sharply, by $4.57 and close to hitting $80, which has put a limit to FOB buyer’s appetite.  One early Nov lifting of an equal ratio cargo is reportedly offered for sale at November CP plus mid-single digit but buyers are not queuing up.  ADNOC released their November lifting acceptances, reportedly with only minor delays.   FAR EAST:  A bullish market in both shipping and products.  The freight increase is undoubtedly propping up all CFR premium. During this week, 23kt Propane for 1h November delivery has been bid up from discounts to a premium of $2/3 on November FEI, this level of premium hasn’t been seen since August.  Off window, quite a few traders are heard to cover shorts for their 1h November delivery program, which will support the premium for a while.  The FEI/MB spread grew to $180ish, which kept the arbitrage window open despite the rising freight.  In the “hot” CFR market Pertamina reissued a buy tender for delivery into Teluk Semangka during 6th to 11th November, the result is yet to know.  Robust demand was also seen from China after arriving back from their holidays. One S.China importer was reported to pay November CP plus over $70 to secure a 1h November delivery of 11+11 kt c3/c4, this even before freights sharp increase. One North China PDH user issued a buy tender to secure half or upto full cargo Propane for delivery during November, which will close on Friday. Other PDHs users also explore possible Propane purchases in November but sellers are cautious in making offers as freight continue to edge up on a daily basis.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Sentiment remains high with Owners, and the freight rate indications being exchanged continue to climb despite the fact that limited clean fixtures are out in the market to support it. Current availability is the key driver with very few, if any ships being marketed in the Atlantic for the whole of October, and also limited vessels available in the East. Additionally plenty of enquiry, plus recent FOB activity is likely to create even more shipping opportunities than were currently seeing. Those players with a larger fleet size, and the ability to free up some of their vessels at the right time and location, are the ones likely to fix at solid levels or secure cargoes at attractive levels. We also saw a change in direction for several vessels that were headed into Europe from the US and now have switched their destination to “East of Suez”. What could have been a short trip leaving tonnage open in the Atlantic, has now dragged more ships out of the basin which could tighten the market further. The recent fixing activity from the Pacific seems to have been short spot trips, delivering at similar dates, and could cause an influx in tonnage opening in the East all at once but we will have to wait and see if options are exercised which could split redeliveries up a little. Weather also playing a role on future availability and dates. No newbuilding LNGC orders reported this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco has announced October CP at $420 for Propane and $435 for Butane, up by $20 respectively from September, which was in line with market expectations. However after the October CP was set, November CP slid by over $25 to $385 only, as compared to previous Thursday.  Crude dipped below $60 this week, amidst the recovery of Saudi production and concerns over global demand.  Qatar petroleum has released their November acceptances with no major delays being reported.  Players are now awaiting other producers’ further acceptances, with a couple of November lifting FOBs Sellers already being seen and asking mid to high single digit premium.     FAR EAST: It’s been a quiet week in the Asian market, mainly due to the ongoing China national holidays.  Sellers of 23kt propane for 1h November delivery are asking November FEI minus $3 to minus $7, while bids heard  at minus $10 level.  The FEI/MB Arb is still wide open, this despite the rising freight and Far East discounts.   This week both India’s IOC and Indonesia’s Pertamina have retendered to buy equal ratio cargos, one is for full month Nov delivery into Ennore and Haldia, and the other is for 6-8th Nov into Teluk Semangka. The result is yet to know but we trust the IOC tender will have high chance of getting awarded because of the greater flexibility in delivery timing.  Despite their holiday’s, Chinese importers are still sniffing for November delivery cargoes, mainly heavy propane ratio as this is for winter heating and petchem use. Late last week one full Propane cargo for early Nov arrival was reported sold at November CP plus low mid 60s basis 1 port E.China, one major China based importer was reported to have resold a 23/0 2h October delivery at October CP plus close to $70 to a PDH user.  One new S.China PDH plant operator was out with a buy tender last Friday for a near prompt delivery of 23kt propane for 20-31 Oct delivery, it didn’t award in the end. Players suspect the buyer will defer its demand into November because of the wide backwardation of over $35 on October to November CP.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The expansion at the Enterprise Terminal has now been completed. The debottle necking completed,  the tie ins made,  and yet the cargos are not there. At one point we were told this expansion would add 175,000 barrels per day, or 10 cargos per month, to the export slate. The reality seems to be an increase of one or two cargos per month. Enterprise stated the product and capability are now there for the increase but the scheduling is where the problem lies and the extra cargos still seem to be well in the future. The propane inventories ended the summer over one hundred million barrels and a level that should lay to rest any fears on product tightness over the winter of 2019/2020. In fact with ever increasing production the idea of a tight product market in the US seems like ancient history.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Another Gastech is behind us, this time leaving many of the visitors with an overflowing impression, quite literally. The LNG market has continued to be flooded with cargo tenders and subsequently shipping requirements, diminishing the prompt vessel availability across all of the basins to the lowest levels we have seen for a long time. Sublet owners, who recently contributed to the excess prompt availability, have become more cautious and started to withdraw some of those positions while increasing their rate ideas significantly. Charterers in need for a flexible cold spot tonnage, especially in the Pacific, have noticed that in order to fix the vessel they have to pay substantially more than a few weeks ago. That said, the Atlantic side has not been as active as the East, and whilst vessel availability is clearly tight, we have to be wary of the limited number of fixtures done in the region. As typical to our LNG industry however, sentiments can swing from one side to another within a week, but at least for now, LNG shipping seems to have hoisted the sails once again. This week we have no LNGC newbuilding orders to report.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS  The draw of 1 million barrels in US inventories was seen as a correction from the previous large builds and strengthened Mt Belvieu prices. The strength was not dramatic and only slightly affected netback values. The arb remains wide open and as we approach winter there is very little to no chance of cargoes being cancelled form the US at these $170pmt October US/FEI arb values. Traders are now back to trading around a month prior to laycan having done deals further out in the wake of the Saudi attack news. Recently seen demand for US butane has been very strong and traders are now looking at a bidding war to try to prise away already programmed tons. This has been attributed to historic seasonal US trade for gasoline blending in the winter, leaving international traders to fight against a historically good domestic trade and making butane availability tight.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG  Inquiries for FOB cargoes of equal ratio split has prevailed in the market during this week but few October liftings are available.  One Asian Major was reported to have resold their November equal ratio cargo at November CP plus $3. On Thursday one Chinese player was out trying to sell their early November lifting of 2/2 ratio at November CP plus $8, but nothing has been concluded yet.   Because to the tightness of MEG supply amidst strong demand, October FEI/CP has been narrowing rapidly. In fact, October CP has surpassed FEI by $5-7 during Thursday’s trading. October CP stands firm at $420, despite crude softening throughout this week. November’s CP is traded at $9-10 below October but we believe it might catch up if the tightness of MEG supply continues.       FAR EAST   The aftermath of the Saudi incident has continuously been supporting the CFR East market price. Traders have been busy securing US origin cargoes to cover their shorts in the SE Asia markets and active bids and trades have been shown up in the window all of this week. FOBs ex MEG for specific dates are being bid at October CP plus from small single digit to teens premium, depending on the ratio and loading dates. 23kt Propane for 2h October delivery has been traded a couple of times at Oct FEI minus $3 to $5.   India’s IOC and BPCL have issued buy tenders consecutively to cover front shorts for October delivery but it seems they were unable to secure prompt availabilities. Indonesia’s Pertamina is reported to have secured an October delivery of equal ratio at October CP plus low mid 40s and one similar cargo for November delivery at high 40s, an additional tender for an evenly split cargo for 1h November delivery into Teluk Semangka remain uncovered.    Taiwan’s FPCC is reported to have awarded their buy tender for a full propane cargo with delivery mid Nov at Nov MOPJ minus high 60s, Hanwha Total is also reported to have award their private tender at November MOPJ minus 80s for 23k propane delivered early November.   Another hot issue this week is that on Wednesday US levied more sanctions against several Chinese companies and individuals. It has aroused players’ attentions in the forward market into China, especially when China is the biggest single destination for absorption of Iranian oil and gas.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: After a larger than expected 2.9 million barrel build inventories have  gone over 100 million barrels for the first time since November 2016. These stocks levels are set to keep Mt Belvieu prices around or below the 33% WTI mark where they are today and thus competitively priced in global markets. After a flurry of interest in US FOBs due to Saudi supply constraint worries led to a jump form 7 cpg done Friday 13th September to 10 cpg done on Tuesday 17th September. Now that the dust has settled it seems the Saudi attacks will have less of an impact on their exports than originally expected and demand for prompt US tons has reduced. However,  in our view, the vulnerability of the Middle East experienced last weekend,  will allow US exporters to remain at or very near capacity for the for see able future.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG:  The incident in Saudi Arabia over the weekend turned the whole market upside down. Tuesday late night Saudi Aramco finally released their October liftings acceptances, this was with only around two weeks delay being reported and minimal cuts heard, this soothed the market sentiment somewhat.  October CP initially surged to $450, up by $100 compared to the previous Friday, only to later plunge to $400 after the acceptance announcement.  We still believe that with the impact of such incident, October CP will hover above the $400 level. In addition, the prompt demand from especially India and Indonesia, means Butane undoubtedly will be maintained at $10-15 higher. At the time of writing, October CP is traded at $410. However, the front strength has slightly changed forward CP swaps into a backwardated structure.  Qatar Petroleum awarded their mid October lifting of full Propane to a Chinese importer at October CP plus small premium.    FAR EAST:  The supply disruption in Saudi has helped support the US origin price. 23k Propane for 1h October delivery was traded at October FEI minus $15.5. A similar cargo for 2h October delivery is being bid at October FEI minus $12 versus offer at minus $5.  With ample supply from the US, October FEI/CP has narrowed to a $5 spread, makes US origin tons even more attractive to Japan and Korean importers.  The US-Feast arbitrage is still wide open, and players are keen to secure equal ratio cargoes ex US, either to cover shorts in own system into SEA, or for better optimization on cargo origin swap.  Off window market, discussions was in a stalemate situation. VLGC freights are increasing due to friction in the MEG and potential increase in additional war risk premium etc.  Meanwhile, some lifters are cautiously programing bearing in mind the Saudi delay in liftings and continually monitoring the loading schedules out of the MEG before taking further decisions.    There are still some buying inquiries for October delivery tons, not only from China but also prompt demand from India and Indonesia.  Some traditional importer still have room to take in middle October delivery Propane heavy cargoes, while the others are now exploring November delivery tons.  Indonesia’s Pertamina issued another buy tender, this time to buy an even ratio cargo to be delivered into Teluk Semangka during flexible October dates which is closing this Friday with validity till following Monday. India BPCL has issued prompt buy tender for a 22/22 delivered during end Sep into early Oct arrival.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: What some thought was to be a quiet week on the chartering front with Gastech in Houston taking many players away from their desks was proved wrong as the spot shipping market turned rapidly with an influx of shipping requirements being issued early this week. The predominant wave of activities are Pacific-driven as vessels find employment with a significant increase in charter rate sentiments compared to the previous week. Spot prices for LNG have increased in both basins as well, and may have contributed to the recent flurry of activities on the spot shipping market.   While charter rate levels spiked up across all vessel sizes as indicated, no newbuilding orders reported this week and the indicative newbuilding price level remains.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As market participants prepare for Gastech in Houston next week, both LNG product and shipping market show some volatility. Delays at Cameron and on top of the low product prices experienced so far this year, have created a sense of shipping length for most of the portfolio players. Today, however, European gas added a new dimension as TTF rose sharply which has resulted in portfolio players holding off and reducing their availability, whether this will end up as a profit making decision is a trader's dilemma as they decide if this is a structural shift or a temporary shift, but Owners should take comfort in the reduced availability. In both basins, requirements are looking at October and November laycans, for both spot or term/multimonth requirements. Rates have dropped slightly on the back of excess availability on the prompt and although is very early to say, it is very uncertain if last year’s highs will be witnessed this year. That said, we do expect some potential tightening towards November, or sooner should today gas price changes be sustainable. There were no Newbuilding orders recorded this week and Secondhand prices have remained stable.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: ADNOC released their October acceptances without any major delay’s or advancements being reported, at the same time it seems they have no spot tons avails.  Qatar Petroleum reportedly to have awarded their early October lifting of a full cargo Propane at October CP minus a small discount to a Chinese Major. Following this, Qatar Petroleum issued yet another tender, this time to sell basis middle October loading a full Propane, closing Monday 16th Sept.  KPC was also reported to award their mid Oct lifting 3/1 cargo as well at some small premium to October CP, which gains value from forward month contango if delivered into Nov.   Compared to full Propane or Propane heavy cargoes, equal ratio cargoes are presently more in favor as there seems more shorts into India and Indonesia.  This week a late October lifting of 2/2 FOB was traded at October CP plus a small premium. Over the week October CP fluctuated with Crude, yet still gained the support from demand driven by the SE Asia market.  At time of writing, October CP is traded at $353 and butane at $13 higher.  November CP maintains a $3-4 contango, reflecting the anticipation of a probable tightness of Non-Us origin cargoes against a better demand in winter.    FAR EAST:  Big gap exists between bid and offer for 23/0 delivered during 1h October, with Seller’s asking Oct FEI minus $21 while Buyer’s at minus $30. This is despite a similar cargo earlier this week was traded at minus $18 off window. Buyer’s appetite is limited, seeing ample US supply and an impending expansion in LPG exports. A Seller with 2h October arrival of full cargo Propane is asking Oct FEI minus $15 but no buyer seen.  One E.China importer is reported to have awarded their buy tender for 23/0 for delivery during 2h October at October CP plus low 50s while another similar cargo was sold at mid-50s into NChina. There are still a few more Propane heavy inquiries, which value still assessed at +50ish.  Pertamina reissued buy tender for two equal-ratio cargos for early Oct and end Oct delivery respectively, the result is yet to reach the market but market players reckon that the early October delivery inquiry might not have been awarded, or the price could be higher than the perceived market level. Latest India’s IOC is reported to have awarded an equal ratio cargo for October delivery at Oct CP plus high 40s.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The US market seems to have found its new normal. Exports are continuing at the 1 million barrel per day level and at a price range between 5.5 and 7 cpg. Domestic Propane prices seem to have settled at approximately 33 percent of WTI and until Winter demand kicks in we expect this to continue. In fact with LPG production so high some are even questioning how much cold weather can actually effect pricing this winter. Another big factor hanging over the US market is how full Asia and Europe are. This is normally a time when end users are pre buying for the Winter and adding demand to exports,  but with discounts well into the future,  this is not happening. Domestic propane inventories increased by 800,000 barrels this week, well below expectations, but putting the total number at 97.8 million barrels.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It’s back to the office after the summer holidays for some and with it the expectation that we ought to be leaving the quieter "shoulder month season" and seeing the influence of winter demand. This week has seen a lot of activity globally, both in the cargo and the shipping market as supply and demand tenders grab traders attention. October laycans are the focus with multiple spot vessel requirements in addition to term vessel interest, although with less vigor than last year. The Pacific has been the busiest region and this may mark a long awaiting increase in activity. The Atlantic market may also see an upturn, Freeport is producing its first cargoes, Cameron is up and running, as well is Corpus train two. It’s this cargo outlook on the back of a limited vessel availability list, albeit growing, that sees rates relativity stable despite low utilization. That said, this week we see a small drop in rates as prompt vessels start to lengthen availability lists. Looking further out, the curve appears to shallow as some Owners come forward to work on late Q4 requirements.  Early days to predict where rates may end the year and we may yet we see a real tightening with the second half of November showing the most promise for Owners. Orders at the yards remain subdued with one order being reported at HHI whilst at the other end of the market two elderly vessels head for scrap.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Another volatile week with Oct CP initially plunging to $346, only to rebound to $357 today, following the crude rise. With several buying tenders into SE Asia, more or less promptly, FOB buying interests surged but few deals have been traded as lifters are awaiting the acceptances to get full picture.  There was one trader bidding Oct lifting at flexible dates for a 2/2 FOB cargo at Oct CP minus $1.  Butane have undoubtedly gained support as most inquiries are mainly for equal ratio split. At the time of writing, Oct butane is traded $372.    FAR EAST: Seemingly slim interest with limited bids/offers in window.  Outside window 23k propane for 1h Oct delivery was reported to have been traded at Oct FEI minus $18/19 CP, this equates to Oct CP plus small digit premium only. 1h/2h Oct maintains at $3 contango but it may easily be erased as additional US exports are scheduled for arrival in Q4.  Otherwise it’s a week with tenders being floated.  India’s IOC issued buy tender for two evenly-split cargoes for delivery during mid Oct and last decade Oct respectively.  Indonesia’s Pertamina have also issued tender to secure two evenly-split cargoes for delivered into Kalbut during late Sep and late Oct respectively, considering both FOB and CFR alternatives.  Taiwan’s FPCC issued a buy tender to secure an early Oct 11/11 or 22/0 arrival. And it was reported to have been awarded at Oct MOPJ minus mid 70’s  One China’s largest Importers issued a buy tender for one full or Propane heavy cargo to be delivered monthly from Oct 2019 to Sept 2020, FEI pricing to be used. Other Chinese importers are exploring Oct arrival cargoes, with equal ratio discussed at Oct CP plus 40s, and Propane or Propane heavy possibly at higher premia as this include PDH users.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: After a brief quiet spell,  demand for FOB cargos has picked up once again. For October, the 4 US Gulf terminals are sold out and any spot possibilities will have to come from the resale of third party barrels. The Enterprise expansion barrels have yet to show up and this is causing us to ask why. Is there a problem the company is not discussing or is it just taking a bit longer than expected.  In the domestic market, propane is holding up above the 30 percent versus WTI  level despite very high inventories. We believe this has to do with vast amounts of propane being bought to hedge the exports but we do not expect this to continue. With this weeks build of 2.9 million barrels, we expect propane prices to fall.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As August comes to a close with the LNG cargo market continuing to underwhelm, owners and charterers circle the dancefloor waiting for each other to make the next move. Portfolio players and traders with length in their fleets, either through trading shorter routes or with pre-secured winter coverage, are growing reluctant to sub-let but continue to be well-placed to pick up the cargoes that do come to market. The result is a general lack of demand for independent tonnage; however, the good news for owners is that vessel availability remains tight particularly in the west, and the east is not awash with vessels despite the usual seasonal build-up. With the imminent start-up of Freeport and the approaching winter demand, the enduring strong sentiment is readily understood.    On the newbuilding front, there were two further orders last week: one fresh order placed by NYK at SHI and an option exercised by Maran Gas at DSME. This brings the YTD total for 2019 to 31 conventional LNGCs, versus 37 for the same period in 2018 and 62 for the full year.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco today announced September Propane CP at $350, this being $20 less than August, Butane September CP came at $360, flat to August.  Paper swaps had been traded higher this week, due to prompt demand from both India and Indonesia for September liftings of equal ratio cargos.  After the September CP announcement, October CP traded at up to $357, October FEI/CP quickly narrowed to $21 from a previous $30ish.  One European trader reportedly sold a 20-25 September lifting of full cargo C3 to a Chinese importer at discount to Oct CP.    FAR EAST: A few deals were concluded in the window this week as traders had to cover shorts.  23k Propane were traded at September FEI minus $11ish. A similar cargo for 1h October delivery were offered at Oct FEI minus $16, buyers are still to come forward.   Indonesia’s Pertamina awarded an evenly split 2/2 delivery into Kalbut during 4-6th October, reportedly at October CP plus high 30s. And new tender for same ratio cargo at 8-10th October delivery into Teluk Semankga has closed but result is yet to be known. India’s HPCL also issued prompt tender for end Aug and Early Sep delivered equal ratio cargoes, which they didn’t manage to award. Later they reissued buy tender for 45kt equal ratio cargo to be delivered during 11 Sep to 5 Oct, and a 21k equal ratio cargo for 21-31 Sep delivery.   Comparatively, the Chinese market appeared quiet this week as most Buyers have already covered their September positions and waiting for September CP announcement before taking October positions. One end September/early October arrival of full Propane is reported to have been sold to China at October CP plus low mid-40s. One E.China petchem user is reported to have purchased 23kt Propane for 2h September delivery at September CP plus low 50s level.  China custom data shows August imports at close to 2mmt, which is the highest monthly import level in 2019 so far.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: USGC: The market mostly shrugged off the 3.7 million barrel build with some assistance from crude. However we are now 23 million barrels over last year and for sure on pace to break the 100 million level. Volumes are still somewhat lack luster as it has priced most of this in and traders are still nursing summer hangovers. With three weeks of over 3 million barrels built per week in US inventories, this has become the new normal. The FOB market in the US continues to be active for end September and early October although more offers have recently been seen than bids. Despite this FOB discussions continue around the 6cpg mark.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS US inventories grew 4 million barrels last week which was above market expectations but the market managed to not lose any further ground from prior to stats. Current inventories stand at 90.5 million barrels a large 22 million barrels over last year. This has traders looking at the weekly propane production. The 4 week average of 2.253 million barrels a day is high. This production coupled with high inventory levels has been keeping Mt Belvieu propane around 30% of WTI. Export capacity from the US has increased this year and if Mt Belvieu remains cheap we could see a large amount of that export capacity being utilised sooner than expected. Traders are wondering if we will see multiple cancellations before the end of the year. Or if the market will continue to support elevated freight rates, and FOB trades slightly above cancellation levels.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: During the past trading week we’ve seen a firming sentiment in all basins, but this has yet to translate into firming rates. The stronger sentiment is mainly driven by a reduction in available tonnage, a number of cargoes to work/ offer on and expectations of strong winter shipping market. Sublets are however keeping the shipping market in check but only for the time being. The sublet tonnage will eventually be required back to its original intended trades which will again set the stage for the independent owners and the winter market.  In other news, Samsung has secured yet another LNGC newbuild order and Global Venture has reached FID on their 10+ MTPA Calcasieu Pass LNG project. We also congratulate Cameron LNG train 1 for starting commercial operations. Next in line may be Freeport Train 1?

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Despite the Brent stands above 60$, LPG paper values doesn’t follow anywhere near closely this week. By time of writing, Sept Propane CP traded at $338 whilst Butane is $10 higher at $348. Saudi Aramco has announced Sept lifting acceptances with some liftings reported to be deferred into 2h Sept and later month lifting, with less supply due to oil cut. Therefore supports front CP and front contango narrowed from $5 to almost flattish.  Other than this, a couple of 1st decade Sept lifting FOB spots have been traded this week at single digit discounts, against the rising freight. This week Baltic has risen amid plentiful shipping inquiries from Indian players and tight supply in 1st decade Sept.    FAR EAST: CFR prices for delivery into Korea/Japan still appears weak, as 23kt Propane for 2h Sep delivery traded at Sep FEI minus $16, which equates to a CFR price of Sep CP plus high single digit this Wednesday. Similar cargo for 1h Oct delivery is offered at Oct FEI minus $12.  With ample supply from US and limited buying interest for US origin, Sep FEI/CP has narrowed rapidly from $28 earlier this week to $20.   During the Thursday window, One Chinese major was bidding a 3/1 cargo for 2h Sep delivery at Sep CP plus $44, meanwhile they are bidding one 3/1 loading 22/23 Sep at Sep CP minus $2 and one 2/2 loading 17/18 Sep at Sep CP minus $3. Another Chinese major bids a 3/1 for Oct delivery at Oct CP plus 43$.  However such bidding ideas are yet to attract seller’s interest, considering current rising freight.  One Chinese major is reported to have covered a 33/11 Sep delivery at Sept CP plus 40ish this week. discussions from traditional importers remain tepid due to high stocks and concerns over weakening domestic prices with the possibility of cheaper Sept CP.    Pertamina issued buy tender for two equal ratio cargoes delivered into Indonesia at 4-6 Oct into Teluk Semangka and 8-10 Oct into Kalbut, FOB alternative are also considerable.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Despite the crude rise and fall, Propane CP has been quite stable at 340ish until Thursday, it dived to $335 at the time of writing and still traded down. Butane CP maintains $14/15 higher and it’s likely to sustain as of better demand from India. Limited lifting inquiries from last decade Aug into early Sep, amid ample shipping length, have exerted pressure on freight.  FOB discussions have been improved to smaller discounts, especially for later Sep lifting cargos, due to weakening freight and slight contango into Oct. Players are still waiting Saudi Aramco’s acceptance to reveal a clearer picture on Sep FOB market.     FAR EAST:  Market remains quiet until Thurs, a flurry of offers appear in window with delivery ranging from 1h Sep into 1h Oct. 23k propane for 1h Sep delivery is offered at Sep FEI minus $23 which equates to Sep CP plus $4! 2h Sep delivery cargo is offered at minus $16 while bid at minus $25. And sellers with 1h Oct cargo are asking Oct FEI minus $9/$10. Off window, 2h Sep propane was reported traded at Sep FEI minus $15 earlier this week. As Us arb to east is still open and weak demand from Europe, we believe lifters will continuingly bring tons and east discussion will still be heavily discounted.    Other than window, some tenders are flowing in the market.  One E.China PDH is reported to issue a buy tender for 23k propane delivered in late Sep, while another E.China petchem user is reported to issue a buy tender for 23k propane monthly delivered from Oct to Dec. There are a few more propane demand in late Sep from other petchem users, but traditional importers are cautious and hesitant to stockpile in such bearish market.  India demand is slowly recovering, with one importer have purchased 23k butane for 2h Sep delivery via tender, and some other inquiry for Sep lifting cargos emerge.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It’s been yet another monotonous start to the week for the LNG shipping market with limited requirements seen.  The national holiday(s) in Asia earlier this week did contribute to a slow start, however trade deals may have also not materialize due to the current softening of LNG prices. There were a few sell tenders which could have developed into shipping requirements, but again they were mostly awarded to Traders/ Portfolio player with length in shipping. The continued limited cross basin arbitrage has also decreased ton/ miles and ensure a relatively decent short-term supply of shipping as vessels fixed on spot for a single voyage are mostly trading within the basin and would return on the  availability list within the span of 2-3 weeks.  Despite this, sentiment and rate expectation remain stable as we move into September. We do feel that traders/ portfolio players are slightly cautious with regards to subletting their tonnage during this period as the majority of market participants expect rates to pick up.  As for multi month charters, we did hear favorable numbers on the last deal concluded and we still do encounter some strong multi month interest from a handful of charterers looking for coverage this winter.  On the Newbuildings, Tsakos Energy Navigation have order up to two vessels (1+1) from Hyundai Heavy industries last week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The market was battered down after inventories on Wednesday after showing a higher than expected build of 3.2 million barrel build for the week ending August 9th 2019. This has left US inventories at 86.5 million barrels, 24% above the same week last year. The way US production is going has lead traders to believe US inventories will exceed 100 million barrels of propane before draw season begins. It has also lead to traders believing that draw season will begin later than the historic October 1st date. US FOB discussions are still above cancellation levels, but with delivered markets looking very weak and discounted, traders are wondering where they can place the tons. The question is if Mt Belvieu propane continues to be cheap, around or below 30% of WTI, will the good value manage to sustain 1.3 million barrels per day or above of exports from the US through winter?

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Weak end user demand mainly coming from North East Asia has held the product price on the floor this past week with the LNG supply overhang still apparent in both basins. However, we have seen more creative chartering opportunities, as spot rates climbed despite the amount of available tonnage, especially from the Pacific. Those Charterers in Europe who are observing the forward pricing curve, are perhaps now considering to float cargoes in the area, which could tie up some tonnage in the basin as we head into the winter months. Owners still remain bullish for winter and multi-month chartering still seems to be the most attractive option for them with healthy appetite for this type of business holding rates strong. However, with the product price remaining low compared to this time last year, it may be unlikely that Charterers will be able to justify the dizzy heights gained by Owners last year if they have a say. Yard pricing remained unchanged since last week, and no new orders have been reported.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: The US market showed weakness after a larger than expected build of 2.8 million barrels. We are now nearly 17 million barrels over last year’s inventory level. This combined with the weakness in crude has made US NGLs weaker. The bearishness in US NGLs has been mirrored by delivered East and West markets. Which carried heavy physical discounts even before the inventory stats were released and larger discounts have been heard since. The effect of this has not yet been reflected in terminalling fees due to quiet FOB discussions. There is skepticism in buying FOBs with so much product in the market. Traders see the potential downside outweighing the potential upside at the moment for spot market trades.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Unexpected plunge in swap market in this week, following the crude. Thurs Sep CP is traded low at $335 only, $35 less than last Thur. Contango into Oct also shrank to $2 from previous $7.  However, butane spread against propane has improved from - $8 to $11, as of better demand and relatively long supply for propane overall. Qatar Petroleum is reported to sell an early Sep lifting full propane cargo to One Chinese buyer at Sep CP with some discounts.   FAR EAST: Very weak sentiment in the market this week. On Thursday window, propane for 1h Sep delivery is offered at Sep FEI minus $15, which equates to Sep CP plus $12, while buyer at minus $30! 2h Sep delivery is offered at $3-3.5 higher but still no buyers seen. Despite such discounts, off window some Japanese and Korean importers reflected with high stock level and they are reluctantly to do more stockpile, therefore such price still faced with downward pressures.   One N.China PDH user awarded their buy tender for 1h Sep arrival full C3 at reportedly Sep CP plus mid-60s. Nevertheless, the discussion level come off quick due to ample supply and softening freight. Bids on propane dropped to 50ish while equal ratio even cheaper as limited buyers available from China. There are some chances that less supply ex Iran might stimulate some demand for substitute cargos, however current poor margins with previous high inventory have exerted pressure and suppressed buyers’ appetites.    Whereas outside China, demand from India seems returning from previous stalemate. One Indian importer is reported seeking butane for Sep delivery, and several traders are procuring late Sep lifting equal ratio spot tons into India.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco announced August propane CP at 370$ down by 5$ while butane CP at 360$ up by 5$, in line with market expectation. Few fobs available from producer on Aug lifting, apart from one trader is reported bought a mid Aug lifting equal ratio cargo from Saudi at Aug CP flat level, to utilize their vessel.   Paper swap is volatile after Aug CP set. Sep CP surged up to 380$ on Wed but came off quick on Thursday, traded flattish to Aug CP at 370$ only. Sep FEI/CP also narrowed down to mid-30s and still under pressure.     FAR EAST: Nothing was concluded in Window this week despite active bids/offers in window. On window 1h Sep propane seller asking Sep CP plus $29, or Aug Balance FEI minus $1, whereas buyers are not seen. 2h Sep seller offers at Sep FEI minus 7.5$ while bid at minus 11$. Off window 1h Sep was reported traded at Sep FEI minus 8.5 to 9$ mid-week. Although forward market in contango structure, abundant front length still exerts pressure on CFR value and buyers are expecting bigger discounts.   Chinese buyers have started exploring Sep delivery cargos. One Nchina PDH buyer has issued tender to secure one full propane cargo during 1h Sep delivery. At the time of writing the result is yet to know. Off window sellers is heard targeted at high 60s to 70s for such cargo.   Indonesia Pertamina is reported to have awarded their latest tender for 10-14th Sep delivered into Kalbut at Aug CP plus low 50s, which alternatively reflected less discounts on FOB netback.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Due to unprecedented delays in the US Gulf during the late Winter and Spring of this year the Arb market enjoyed a very good few months. Many traders pondered whether this was precursor to going back to the future of the export Arb or simply a short term outcome of unusual circumstance. As the market now has returned to a more normal summer market, it seems it may be more the latter.    In the US inventories built at close to the expectation of 1.4 million barrels. However this  did not stop the wacky markets between LST and Enterprise. With LST losing a substantial amount of price on the  last day of the month, they now start August at parody. We do not expect this to last but only time will tell. Ethane reached single digits on the week for the first time  but that was also just for the July barrel. In August Ethane may  test the single digits again.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The LNG prices, particularly the North East Asian prices have been relatively low, reportedly due to limited demand from the end-users. Despite the flat LNG prices, there has been more activity in the LNG ship chartering market. Vessels have been recently fixed for single voyages and multi-months charters for August and September deliveries. Charter rates have been relatively firm, despite owners facing stiff competition for each and every chartering requirement. All eyes are on the fixing levels for September cargoes as these are currently being negotiated. These would clearly indicate the direction the shipping market is moving as we approach Q4 where traditionally the increasing LNG demand due to winter may lead to a number of players seeking to play the contango.   Despite the strong sentiments for LNG vessel newbuilding activity recently, no new orders were reported this week. However, this year is due to be an interesting one as we expect the yard slots to be taken up in due course.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERCIAS A 1.6 million barrel build has done what it can to help a US-FEI arb. Traders feel that US product inventories will approach 1 hundred million barrels before the start of the demand season . Terminal expansion discussions continue to ramp up, but in the current market the terminalling fee discussions are edging towards cancellation levels. This may or may not be affecting the speed of potential export growth which looks to have slowed. Product traders are looking at FOB opportunities, and unless they have their own freight , the arb does not make sense. Traders are hoping for an imminent freight decline to make arb cargo trades workable.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Despite the crude rise earlier this week and improved demand, August swaps was traded under pressure at $360, $15 less than our last report. September CP still maintains at $3-4 contango for the time being. FOB market appeared quiet this week, both for cargo and freight trades. Some players with shipping length are reportedly looking for possible spot cargoes to utilize their ships. With softening freight and improving premia in Eastern market, FOB discounts have narrowed and today one trader was seen offering their late Aug Yanbu lifting 2/2 ratio asking Aug CP plus $5 (Yanbu discount to apply), while the last deal for similar cargo was done at CP minus single digit.     FAR EAST:  Window bids/offers still roam at discount levels.  On Wednesday a 23k Propane for 2h August was traded at August FEI minus $4. A similar cargo for same period, today was offered at minus $2 and cargo for 1h Sep offers at minus $5 basis Sep FEI, yet no bids was seen.  Earlier this week, the strong MB and firm freight squeezed the arbitrage value but latest stock data with a considerable build has enable the economy to return again for Eastern trades.  Off window enquires have been rather active. One EChina PDH user awarded their buy tender for 23k Propane delivered in 2h Aug at Aug CP plus mid high $60s, in addition, an other EChina cracker user was reported to have awarded their buy tender for 22k Propane for delivery end Aug into Taixing at Aug CP plus $60s, even if their original tender demand was for upto 44k Propane.  FPCC has issued a spot tender to buy a 33/11 or 44/0 for delivery during 11-15th Sep, the result is not yet to known.  Pertamina reportedly awarded one 2/2 for their mid Sep demand into Teluk Semangka, and are still looking for one more.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It has been another active week on the shipping side, as we have witnessed a number of fresh requirements from both the East and the West of Suez. Various cargo tenders have been keeping Charterers and Owners busy especially in the Pacific, although these tenders usually yield only shorter one voyage spot fixtures. There are still a handful of open prompt vessels competing for the next business and thus rates have remained steady this week. Looking forward, we still see a few Charterers trying to find the perfect vessel to cover the upcoming winter period and thus multi-month rates have been holding strong but only a few deals have been concluded. On the cargo side, the aforementioned sell tenders have kept the supply high and thus LNG prices low, a tricky situation to many given the relatively firm shipping market. The uncertainty of the shipping outlook, together with the comparatively bearish cargo market, has created a lot of discussion around freight derivatives and the possibility to adopt them in wider perspective into LNG shipping – something that will be very interesting going forward. On the newbuilding front, SK Shipping has been confirmed placing an order with HHI for one 180,000cbm LNGC with planned delivery in 2021.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco released their August acceptances with several equal ratio cargoes for early month lifting while the predominant heavy Propane at end month. KPC is reported to have awarded their 13/14th August FOB sale tender at August CP minus mid/high teens.  FOB values have now been under pressure for a while with freight standing firm and stagnant demand from end user Buyers.  However, with contango into forward market and possibly less supply from Iran, we believe the situation might improve.  At time of writing, August CP is traded at $3. Contango into Sep has narrowed but still maintained at $3, compared to last week’s $7-9.    FAR EAST:  The market is recovering from the quietness of last week with a handful of deals concluded, off window mainly. Full cargo Propane for 2h Aug delivery is reported to have been traded at FEI minus low teens, while half cargo at minus high single to $10. 23k propane for 1h Sep delivery is reported to have done at FEI minus $5.5.
