With front length being almost absorbed, this has enhanced the discussing levels gradually.  Nevertheless, the FEI discount levels may stay for the time being with continued abundant arb tons from US and still limited outlets.  For Non-Us cargo, one E.China PDH Buyer have tendered to buy 2h August Propane, result is yet to be known. A few other Chinese petchem users are also looking for Propane for similar arrival period. One Chinese traditional domestic importer is currently inquiring for an equal ratio cargo with 2h August delivery. In addition, one SEA importer explores for heavy Butane or half cargo butane for 2h August delivery.  FPC awarded their term tender for one full cargo Propane per month from Oct 2019 to Sep 2020 at MOPJ minus about high 70’s.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The softening trend of recent weeks seems to be bottoming out. LNG price environment remains low, particularly JKM when compared with the 10’s seen this time last year. The spot arbitrage between European reloads and North East Asian has widened this week showing glimmers of light, yet insufficient to buck the general trend seen this year and leaving traders little margin to accommodate the demands of the recent freight levels. Looking to the East, the past week has seen a notable pick-up in activity on the spot and while the shipping market is generally bullish as shipowners look towards the winter, it is not far-fetched to suggest that the weak prompt that has been threatening to continue throughout Q3 may be coming to an end.   Tonnage for winter coverage remains the priority for many traders and portfolio players alike. The recent string of multi-months fixtures may have contributed to the recent heightened bull run which drove rates up to levels typically seen in winter months. These are fixtures meant primarily for winter cargoes and access to worldwide flexibility, suggesting that the charter rate increases are more sentiment driven rather than reflecting actual fundamentals. All eyes will be on the actual gas demand from the North East Asian importers as we inch further into Q3 which could certainly drive freight costs beyond levels the market has seen this year.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: After a 3 month run of open arbs, rising freights,  and a general good feeling, the window  has been slammed shut. For the second week in a row, the inventories in the US showed a much smaller build than the industry had expected. A week ago the US showed a small draw and this week the inventories showed a small build of 500,000 barrels. This has occurred at a time when most were expecting builds in the magnitude of around 2 million barrels a week,  and combined with these expectations,  the US market has firmed considerably. We are still believers in the  growing US production and nececessity to export,  but afor now  traders have become much more skeptical and th netbacks have fallen back to cancellation levels.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: LNG cargo market remains soft with Far East DES price at low levels and with East to West arbitrage firmly shut, yet this week more shipping activity appeared with a few spot requirements mainly witnessed east of Suez. Sentiment seems to be picking up as players prepare for winter and the latest sub fixtures concluded suggest that we might see rates steadily firming. In the West, things remain relatively muted as closed arbitrage encourages limited cross basin trades and give some sublet availability, putting pressure on prompt rates. The scenery completely changes when we looking into Q3 cargoes where Owners are indicating more robust figures. On term, interest from Charterers on multimonth and multiyear business remains strong and it will be interesting to see the outcome of these requirements within the next few weeks. There have been no new orders reported this week and newbuilding prices remain stable.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: AMERICAS: Enterprise Products issued a press release this week stating that in addition to their 175,000 barrel expansion coming on line in September of this year, they would have another expansion of 260,000 barrels per day commencing third quarter 2020. When completed this would give Enterprise a capacity to load 1.1 million barrels per day of LPG or 60 VLGC cargoes per month. It seems hard to imagine where all this product will go but one thing that seems certain in LPG is the product always seems to find a home. Closer to the present the Gulf Coast is gearing up for its first storm of the season, Current forecasts have the storm missing the Texas export Terminals and going into Louisiana but precautions are being made none the less. With Enterprise and Targa finally recovered from the winters disruption they are holding their breath and hoping this storm does not hit.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: There are plenty of FOB spot cargoes available from producers and traders as resales, some of which have already been concluded. Qatar Petroleum reportedly awarded a full Propane for 31th July to 2th Aug lifting at Aug CP minus high single digit. Kuwait closed their sale tender for a Butane heavy cargo for  lifting 11-12 August today with result yet to be known. ADNOC released their August acceptances with some liftings being advanced.  Considering front high freight rates and forward contango market, no wonder lifters like to nominate and get latter liftings. Trader resale are also being actively discussed for cargoes across the whole month. One trader is offering early Aug lifting 2/2 at minus 10$ in window as well.  At the time of writing, August CP has risen by nearly $20 to close to $390, and September at $8 higher.    FAR EAST: Supply appear to be in abundance. We have seen offers for 2h August Propane at AFEI minus $5-6, while bids are at minus $10.  The Origin spread has enlarged dramatically from barely zero to small digits three weeks ago, to back around $20s, mirroring the length of US tons in the front.  With large stocks and slow domestic consumption in July, Chinese Buyers have remained quiet for 1h August, that was until end this week. One domestic importer and one PDH user were reported to have covered with some spot purchases. PDH users are now mainly exploring 2h Aug delivery tons.  Despite the high freight and with limited buyer interests, price discussion levels have come off significantly from 70s in last two weeks to 50s for Propane, while equal ratio is even lower.  China’s 2nd biggest LPG importer has issued term tender to purchase one 2/2 or 3/1 cargo monthly from October 2019 to June 2020. The result is yet to know.  FPCC awarded their buy tender to secure a 11/11 for mid August delivery at Aug MOPJ minus around $105. Following this, FPCC issued term tender to cover 22/0 or 44/0 monthly with delivery from October 2019 to September 2020, which closes this Friday. Last time they’ve awarded one 44/0 monthly from July 2019 to June 2020 at MOPJ minus low 70s.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The 4th of July traditionally marks the middle of the summer and the market seems to be reflecting this as well. Inventories are building as expected,  and with this weeks build of 1.3 million barrels it seems almost certain that inventories will peak at  over 100 million barrels when the winter season officially starts on October 1st. Production is maintaining over 2 million barrels a day and exports are maintain over 1 million barrels per day. In South America, Gasco, the owner of Gasmar, and Enlasa announced their plans for a new fully refrigerated floating storage has been approved. Construction is scheduled to start in March of 2020 and the project should be completed in the 2nd quarter 2022. The tank will be 45000 cubic meters and the imports will be handled by Gasmar.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The LNG shipping market continues to pull owners in different directions, with the soft cargo market weighing on prompt business while a flurry of term requirements maintain longer-term confidence. The week began with a slight upturn in Asia spot pricing and the prospect of an inter-basin arbitrage, but such hopes were short-lived and had little impact on shipping before margins narrowed again – prompt availability persists and may creep steadily higher over the coming month as current charters end and more sublets appear. It’s a different story on multi-year business, with several majors and portfolio players coming out for tonnage from next year leading to a surge of activity, and sentiment remains firm. Between prompt pessimism and longer-term optimism, owners and charterers face some interesting decisions over their winter strategies.   Newbuild prices remain unchanged and no further reports of any new orders this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: As far as deals are concerned, it has been a quiet week in the MEG. The big news was the announcement of the Saudi Aramco Contract Price for July of USD 375/MT for Propane and USD 355/MT for the Butane. The Yanbu discount was set at USD 13 pmt, reflecting the strong VLGC freight market. Forward numbers have been dropping throughout the week, with a small rise at the end of the week, basically shadowing the Crude futures. Most MEG based producers have additional cargoes for sale, with 2 of them having floated sales tenders. One being 3 x 22+22 kt loading 30-31 July, 25-26 Aug and 15-19 Sept, respectively. The other being for 45 kt c3 loading 31 July/02 Aug. It will be interesting to the outcome of these. In addition, India based importers are trying to delay their contractual MEG FOB volumes, because of the slowing down of import requirements.   FAR EAST: It is not, nor has it been a busy week in the Eastern CFR markets. With the HK LPG conference having completed last week, there was hopes for an active return but this was quickly squashed. The petchem demand is very low with cracker turnarounds in August, so no reprieve from that side. The prices in the East continue to be under pressure, which will likely continue with Indian slowdowns, excess MEG supply and US origin cargoes still arriving at pace. Strong VLGC freight’s doesn’t make life easier for Sellers or Buyers and the tariff’s just continue the inefficiencies. Propane still enjoy strong demand from PDH operators, which is expected to continue for the near term, at least.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The overall sentiment in both basins remained steady, but shipping requirements saw a slight decline compared to the previous weeks. The fundamentals of the current trades in both East and West of Suez are still unchanged, as the handful of recent fixtures concluded were intra-basin businesses.  Shipping rates in the Pacific are taking a slight dip and the Atlantic has also seen lesser trades however not enough to justify a drop in rates due to shipping availability being limited and more balanced than the East. Despite the slowdown on the spot, the multi months, term and forward fixing requirements remain fairly strong with Owners standing firm and not submitting to pressure of the current market.  Nevertheless, with Brent prices picking up, more cargo tenders anticipated to come out for Q3-Q4 2019 and seasonal demand in preparation for winter, we expect to see spot activities increase again. Newbuild prices remain unchanged and no further reports of any new orders this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Flat price spiked up from mid-week following the crude price rise, buoyed by the larger decline on crude stock and the concerns on oil supply over the tension between US-Tehran. At the time of writing, Jul CP traded at $376, while Jul FEI at $421. Aug swap number is being volatile, followed tightly at flattish level to July at the moment. But it seems too early to judge if it’s into a contango or backwadation structure, mirroring player’s sentiment on future uncertainties. Jul CP is expected to be announced by this Sunday, and Saudi Aramco is reported to have a mid/2h July lifting 2/2 cargo available.   FAR EAST: With the IHS conference held in HK this week, and the last week before July CP announced, window appears quiet.  On Tue 23kt propane for 1H Aug delivery is traded at Aug FEI plus 1.5$. One fob seller is offering 17-21 Jul lifting 2/2 at discount of 5$, however difficult to entice buyer’s interest as freight still hovering at high 70s level. And propane for 2h Jul was bid at Jul FEI plus $4 while 1h Aug at Aug fei flat only, reflecting the length in in forward market. One North China petchem user have purchased a full propane cargo for 1H Aug delivery reported at CP plus 70s. We expect into Aug China petchem demand to be robust as SP chemical cracker is stockpiling feedstock for the cracker, with all PDHs running at good margin, far better compared to the retailing demand. Indonesia Pertamina issued buy tender for a 3/1 cargo delivered to Kalbut at 9-11th Aug while result was yet to hear. Taiwan FPCC awarded their buy tender for 44kt C3 for 1-10th Aug delivery at Aug MOPJ minus $80.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Mt Belvieu prices are still affected by the weekly stock numbers. This week Mt Belvieu rose after the, 1 million barrel less than expected 1.4million barrel build. International traders cannot ignore the Mt Belvieu price reactions to the weekly inventories, but the feeling is that whether inventories get to 90million or 100million barrels, stocks will be plentiful for winter. Export discussions have been quiet due to an industry conference in Hong Kong and FOB buying ideas have been declining by the day in line with the declining arbs and stagnant freight.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco released their July acceptance over the weekend, with some Butane liftings being advanced. It is reported that the producer is offering equal ratio cargos for July lifting with ample Butane stock. July CP swaps remained flat most of the week, until Thursday afternoon when it rose to $360, shadowing the crude rebound. Not sure if freight has reached the ceiling at $80 but the continuous increment on shipping costs have squeezed the margins, more so when considering current weak demand from India and China. Buyer are asking mid-teens or even higher discounts on FOB.   FAR EAST: Plenty of deals were concluded in the window during this week. 23kt propane for 2h July delivery was traded at Jul FEI plus 3-6$, which equates to July CP plus low mid 50s’. FEI/CP still maintains at 50ish, thanks to the soaring freight. Off window inquiries into China are quite sluggish, thus the spread between US and Non-US origin has been narrowing quickly.   Apart from window deals, a handful of tenders are ongoing. SP Chemical awarded their buy tender to one Chinese major importer at July CP plus 60s for 23k propane, SP Chemicals are reported to be looking for another cargo for end July delivery, for use in their cracker. Following that, Dongguan Juzhengyuan was also reported to have secured Propane from the largest Chinese importer at July CP plus 50s. FPCC awarded their buy tender for 11/11 during 16-20th July delivery into Mailiao at July MOPJ minus mid 80s. Indonesia Pertamina has closed their term tender for 2 full cargos for delivery January to December 2020, result is yet to known.  Having said this, the majority of spot demand is driven by petchem for Propane, buying interest from traditional importers is pretty slim, with only one Chinese importer reported to have purchased an 11/11 cargo at July CP plus around 50$.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The US supply keeps on coming! Gaining 3.4 million barrel build last week was slightly (around 1 million barrels) above trader expectations. These larger than expected builds and general bearish sentiment in Mt Belvieu has not lead to higher terminalling fee discussions. Skyrocketing freight rates have kept product netback values around 9cpg US-FEI based on flat price. Which in itself is bullish for prompt delivered markets as the arbs are supporting strong freight values from the US. There is trepidation around terminalling fees. Buyers not willing pay… and seller not willing to buy… through flat price values. The trader sentiment is that f it makes sense on paper then it can work. With the outlook for Mt Belvieu prices bearish through high supply. The question is: Does bearish Mt Belvieu lead to a wider arb, and what freight level can it maintain?

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The spot shipping market appears to have become subordinate as Charterers have their eyes on the autumn-winter market and in some cases multiyear coverage. Winter coverage often ends up in discussions for a 1yr TC vs the requested 6 or 9 months TC, due to pricing and owners reluctance to take «shoulder months» risk. It will be interesting to see how these year and multiyear discussions pan out over the next few weeks.  Last week was relatively active East of Suez,  but with good availability of vessels, rates remained stable. Markets were quieter West of Suez, but availability within this basin is very limited.  «News of the week» was that Anadarko has taken FID on Mozambique for 12,8 MTPA which could easily translate into a requirement of about 12-16 vessels.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Despite strong and increasing  freight, the arb remains open from the US to Europe and Asia. Production and exports remain at record levels and we expect this to continue going forward. In fact it is hard to see the scenario changing anytime soon unless demand begins to waver.  However, with prices so low compared to the alternatives,  this is not something we expect to happen. Propane inventories rose 2.8 million barrels for the week ending June 7th which slightly above trader expectations, and puts the total number on track to reach over 100,000,000 barrels by October 1st , 2019.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Summer months are upon us, traditionally a period where incremental demand for LNG depends bit more on how hot the weather is. Far East DES prices remain low, at around $4 per mmbtu, hardly a conducive environment for spot trading. During last weeks, demand pattern and shorter trades led to increased availability of sublet vessels from various projects, importers and exporters alike. Hence, the recent firming charter rate in both basins came to a halt. This should all be temporary as the market is expected to firm again as we start working the more autumn dated cargoes leading up to winter.   On the newbuilding side, Maran Gas Maritime hit the headlines yet again with another LNG vessel order at DSME for delivery within the first half of 2022. Samsung Heavy Industries also announced last Friday that they secured another two orders for LNG vessels, to be delivered in 2022.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: After the large price falls throughout this week, Crude rebounded on Thursday afternoon, trickered by the two tanker explosions in the Gulf of Oman.  Following this, LPG Propane prices rose to $348, reviving a bit from overnight’s slide to below $340.  Butane maintains a discount of about $20 against Propane, which is (still) unusual for a typical summer season. This is a testament to the fact that Butane’s length from producers continue.  With ample supply from Middle East and sluggish demand from end users, July CP is still under pressure. Add to this the seemingly ever increasing freight rates, this has killed many buyers’ appetite, mid-teens discounts appear insufficient to trigger speculative trades as well.  Adnoc released their July acceptances with some liftings being advanced. Qatar Petroleum issued a sales tender for 7-9th July lifting on full propane cargo basis. Saudi Aramco is reported to still have a late June 2/2 cargo available for sale.    FAR EAST: Quiet week with only a few physical deals being concluded this week.  Off window a 23kt Propane cargo for 2h July delivery changed hands at July FEI plus $6-$8, which equates to July CP plus mid high 30s.  Non-US origin equal ratio cargoes are assessed at a similar value, while Propane is still at a premium of plus 50s level, this mainly driven by PDH demand which still enjoy substantial profit margins in an otherwise sluggish market.  The forward traded market into August is currently at a slight backwardation, as the front still gains support due to delays caused by US freeport FM and Nederland turnarounds.  Some players expect the premiums to come off further with the anticipation of plentiful arbitrage cargoes reaching Eastern markets in August, along with cheaper MB price and a perceived weaker demand in the East.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Propane inventories resumed their seasonable build , increasing this week by 2.3 million barrels. At this pace inventories should peak at over 100 million barrels by the end of September. This level should ensure more than enough inventory to support a cold winter, as well as maximum exports,  even with the export expansion at Enterprise which will come on line in the third quarter. This high inventory level is also effecting prices, pushing propane levels down to less than 35 percent of WTI. This normally is good for the Arb however high freights are hampering US Gulf exports. In South America, Brazilian demand continues at their normal winter pace.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: This last week have seen a nose dive in prices of LPG from the MEG. It started almost to the minute of June LPG CP prices being announced, by Crude falling sharply on the last trading last week, only to fall even more Monday of this week. While the fall in Crude prices have been sharp, equaling nearly 13 pct. The drop in LPG prices have been even larger, using July’s traded CP over the same period, equaling about 17 pct. We are today in a situation where the traded July Propane CP is at 343, June CP confirmed at 430, this means that the market expect Propane CP to drop by a massive 20 pct. The spot physical price have dropped even more with close to a handful of deals done at discount to July CP. The discounts ranged from high single digit to high teens. The Butane price have been hit ever harder than Propane and it seems that this pricing trend is set to continue with the market being awash with Butane right now.   FAR EAST: The pricing trend in the Eastern markets have mirrored that seen in MEG. While window deal(s) have been near absent this week, one was done earlier today where a Marcus Hook 23/00 1h July was confirmed at July FEI +6, a number of physical deals was confirmed. Market chatter refers to 1 cargo of 22+22 to East China and another of 11+11 to a similar destination with arrival 2nd hf July was concluded at equivalent of July CP netbacks in the minus 30’s and a 22+22 kt cargo for arrival SE Asia early July was heard done at equivalent of July FOB minus mid teens. It feels like end users are taking this opportunity to fill their storages with cargo at time when prices are perceived to have reached bottom, or near thereto. Sellers have had to play ball as the high freights have made it financially impossible to sit vessels and hope for higher prices, at today’s Baltic the VLGC cost of sitting just 1 day is in excess of USD 1.25 PMT. For Propane there are some relief with Propylene trading at close to USD 1,000 PMT in the East and Propane being landed considerably below USD 500 PMT, very large margins are being achieved by the PDH plant operators and we have now seen such operators tendering for cargoes with arrival from end June till end July.  With US volumes seeing an even larger FOB price adjustment, it will be interesting to see where this market will take us in the next 1 to 2 months.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The LNG spot market continues to delight buyers and dismay sellers, with delivered cargo pricing slipping further in Europe and hitting a [3]-year low in the Far East. On-shore storage remains high and the East/West arbitrage is firmly shut, leading to fewer fresh requirements and the squeezing of trading margins. The prompt shipping market has in turn ceased strengthening and may be moving towards a shallow decline: the few recent fixtures completed suggest a slight drop in headline rates, albeit with overall structures that retain elements of positioning and repositioning. However, the view is quite different further out, as the relatively weak hands held by LNG sellers and shipowners today may herald a loaded deck tomorrow. The longer-term ton-mile story remains strong: the first cargo has left Cameron and Prelude is expected to follow suit imminently with more to come, and there is plenty of growth potential offered by an average voyage distance today that is down 10% against long-term levels. Add in to the mix a few other “ifs” and “maybes” that the present market has produced, such as the scope for floating storage if the market enters a contango or for reloads out of a full Europe if the arbitrage opens wide, and the firm and strengthening sentiment of owners towards longer-term charters makes sense.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The US propane inventories showed an unexpected drawdown today of 100,000 barrels. This drawdown was completely unexpected and very far from the consensus view of a build of 2 million barrels. Under normal circumstances,  this would have caused the propane market to spike upwards but with crude falling so fast and so hard it meant that propane would not fall as much and propane did firm compared to WTI closing today at 39 percent of WTI. General belief is that that this is a correction from prior weeks and that next week should once again show a build of close to 2 million barrels. Bottom line is that there is enough inventory to support, domestic cracking, retail and exports for the foreseeable future. In other news US terminals are continuing their catch up from last months delays. Enterprise expects to be caught up in early June and Targa by late June. In Canada, Alta Gas completed their first export from their new facility at Prince Rupert Island, British Colombia. They had a few normal start up delays but overall the terminal performed well and the spec was perfect. All going well Alta gas hopes to have 30 VLGC propane cargos a year from the new terminal.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: We are a few days away from June, which will mark the beginning of the Northern Hemisphere summer months. Although we are only reaching the opening of the summer ‘’peak’’ demand period, it is already proving to be a quite different setup for this summer in the LNG market compared to same time last year, predominantly driven by the sluggish cargo demand and ample supply, pushing the LNG prices close to annual lows. This seems to have caught up with the prompt spot LNG shipping market too as we have recorded only a handful of fresh requirements across the basins, halting the hike of the freight rates for now. Shipping availability has also increased, as we have seen a number of sublets appearing, possibly putting some pressure on the spot freight rates in the upcoming weeks. It is quite a different story on term requirements however, as owners are still holding on to their strong views about the second half of this year, supported by the fact that we see a steady flow of interest for multi-month charters from different LNG players and expect more LNG volume to come online. On the newbuilding front, Hyundai Heavy Industries confirmed late last week to have secured an order for two 180kcbm LNGC newbuilds, increasing the order tally for 2019 to a total of 22.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: The highlight of the week was the announcement of Saudi Contract Prices for June of $430 for Propane and $415 for Butane. At the time of announcement, this was more or less in line with expectations. However, as the week have moved on, it become obvious that there are/were substantial unsold FOB volumes still to be placed. These volumes are from producers and from traders as well Some of these have now been cleared but at large discounts to CP, ranging from high single digit to high teen’s. This price dive has been aided by the continued strength in the VLGC freights. Arriving in the office Monday morning, we were presented with a near contango situation for the balance of the year but this quickly changed whereby backwardation has once again reared it’s ugly head, especially so for Butane. It is reported that Iran LPG export volumes this month will reach 550 kt, or more.   FAR EAST: It has not really been an active trading week, tough some deals were concluded. A WAF origin cargo was sold into East China for 1st half July arrival and a window deal for 23 kt c3 1st half June at June FEI plus 8 was done. These deals are more or less representative of the market developments this week. While these deals point to a CP netback of lower than minus 20, it should not surprise anyone that this downward pressure on CFR values more than likely will continue for some time. The realization that slowing increase in demand from the 2 biggest import markets, combined with continued strong Iranian exports and new volumes from US, Canada and Australia, mean that Eastern markets are very well supplied.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Another volatile week as flat values continued sliding, following the crude.  June propane CP is now trading at $424 at the time of writing, almost $100 less than May CP. Butane is traded at $18 less.  KPC is reportedly awarded their 4/5th June 2/2 at June CP minus mid high single digit.  Qatar tendered to sell a 3/1 for 26/28th June lifting at the pricing on BL dates, with the backwardation to July CP being at more than teens this doesn’t look attractive to buyers unless it comes with an attached substantial discount, more so considering the high freight and sluggish demand in Eastern CFR markets.    FAR EAST: Premiums has come off quickly this week as US export resumes operation and supply tensions getting eased. On Thursday a handful of deals was concluded in the window. 23k propane for 2h June delivery was traded at June FEI plus $11 and July FEI plus $12, while similar cargo for 1h July was done at July FEI plus $6, which reveals the forward length.  There are some cargos being placed into China at a lower premium this week. Market appears long with abundant equal ratio cargos, some of which being surplus from India importers. Propane is maintaining it’s higher value with requirement from PDH buyer. 23k propane was sold at June CP plus low 50s while 11/11 was done at $15-20 lower. One domestic importer is reported to have resold a 2/2 cargo for 2h June delivery at June CP plus 30s level.  Indonesia’s Pertamina appear to have awarded their two 2/2 cargoes for July delivery at June CP plus high 20s to low 30s.  FPC awarded their spot tender for a 33/11 cargo delivered during 1st half July at July MOPJ minus around $105. Previously they’ve awarded their term tender reported at MOPJ minus 70s for 44k C3 monthly from July 2019 to June 2020.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The propane market for sure did not like the stats this week and combined with falling crude oil, made for an ugly day losing over 2.25 CPG. Overall propane inventories are getting rather high @ 65.8 million 48 of which is in the Gulf Coast.    FOB USGC terminalling fees are bid at 7.5cpg while offers are in the double digits for June cargoes. This wide bid/offer level is attributed to window premiums in the East market. These cash premiums remain in the single digits at the moment. This means that traders are reluctant to sell FOB US at a flat netback US/FEI levels. One thing is for , sure as long as market remains in backwardation l, stock building will not start and the entire market knows it must before the winter season.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Rates continued to edge upwards this week with a small yet persistent increase. Demand for cargo appears to have waned again and it’s become quite apparent that freight rates have begun their own journey and delinked from cargo prices. This lack of correlation between the cargo and freight market is highly irregular and has many market players perplexed when assessing multi-month indications. A small yet significant shopping spree for Q3 and Q4 cover has occurred over the past couple of weeks and has left less than a handful of different Owners with flexible tonnage available for the course of 2019. Although the number of multi-month fixtures this year is less when compared to 2018, it is worth noting that this time last year marked the commencement of Charterers taking winter coverage and what followed was a rapid change in the freight market. Cargo prices last summer where very different to today’s but with European regasification slots filling up fast it could be ton-time that dominates the headlines this summer. Availability remains fair with sufficient vessels to serve anticipated demand on the prompt but with more commissioning cargoes coming online in the near future this landscape is likely to change. New build prices take a tick up to 189 this week although orders through Q2 have been slower than the past two quarters.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Delays , delays, delays. Seems the Houston Ship Channel cannot rid itself from the huge magnitude of delays that have occurred this year. First it was fog, then two terrible explosions at two different locations, and last week a collision between a tanker and several barges. The effects of these delays had huge ramifications in the Asian markets and the effects of which are still being felt. Asia is now very dependent on US exports and delays in the US Gulf result in large premiums being paid in Asia. The Asian market is also complicated by the 25 percent tariffs on US product going into China  which has in turn put a premium on non US origin product. On the domestic front the US Propane market showed a weekly build of 2.7 million barrels the majority of which was in the US Gulf. Production came in well over 2 million  barrels per day and domestic demand showed an all time low. Going forward we expect lower US prices and the arb to remain wide.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco released their June acceptances, and it appears that there are some shortage on C3 supply. Lifters who have full C3 liftings get delays while the rest with equal ratios are more comfortable with dates as per nominated. There are plenty of equal ratio cargoes are available in the FOB market and the offer level for 2h June lifting has come off to discount level.  KPC issued a sales tender for a 4/5 June lifting 2/2 c3/c4, result is not known yet.  Indian importers are also reported to postpone/resell some June lifting FOBs.  Paper swap values have been volatile this week. US stock buildup and higher production figures than expected has smashed the market values.  June CP once traded at $480 earlier this week, only to plunge below $450$ and then slightly rebound to $455 at time of writing. Butane is assessed $22 cheaper but with the length on Butane we expect the spread to expand.  FAR EAST: Due to the minor delays caused by the collision in Houston ship channel over the weekend, the June CFR market has tightened, buyers has been buying in/off window to cover front shorts. 23kt propane for 1h June was traded in window at June FEI plus $53, last time such a high premium was achieved is two years back.  2h June CFR market is less tight but Japanese buyers are actively covering in at levels of June FEI plus $25-30.  Comparatively, China importers have been less active this week, main buyers have been PDH operators. Sluggish demand from the domestic sector is killing extra speculative interest. Traditional importers are cautiously monitoring their inventories and sales before deciding whether to buy additional tons, taking into consideration the front premium and intermonth spread between June/July.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Over the past week, LNG Shipping rates have been strengthening on basic market fundamentals, both east and west of Suez. We have seen tightness on modern tonnage and in addition to firmer rates, ballast bonus sentiment is close to roundtrip economics. However, the cross-basin arb is still very much closed. The question therefore is, will this firmer trend continue through the summer and into the autumn or will we have a repeat of last year’s development, where spot rates increased in June, but came of slightly ahead of August?   Going forward, there are quite a few scheduled redeliveries where some need to drydock, but they are also getting good attention from charterers for potential autumn/winter coverage.    DSME logged one LNGC NB this week, although it’s a little uncertainty around the price, it appears to have been a slot that was priced some time ago.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: It has been quite an active week for LNG Shipping. Spot hire rates have increased on the back of several cargoes / requirements in both basins. In addition to the rise in rates, there is a significant push from Owners to cover fuel cost on positioning, as well as improvements on ballast bonus figures. The availability list has also seen a reduction; however, we are far from being “short” shipping, but rather «balanced» as we currently do not foresee any big challenges for Charterers looking to secure a ship for 1H June. Also, due to a weak JKM index versus a steadier NBP, the arbitrage to the East has been closed for quite some time and with most cargoes trading intra basin, ships that are fixed are likely to return to the market shortly. Nonetheless, the current situation looks to favor Owners and we may see the spot market firming further.       Newbuild prices remain unchanged and no further reports of any new orders this week.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Earlier this week May Propane CP has been under downward pressure at 430ish and rebounded mid- week. At the time of writing, May CP is traded at 450$. However, butane CP value has dropped significantly and traded at $15 less than propane, which is irregular in a summer season. One main reason is less demand from both Indian and China, and the other being more Us butane into east available now.    FAR EAST:  1H/2H June backwardation is widening. Bids for 23kt propane for 1h June delivery has edging up to June FEI plus 37$ on Thurs window while no offer seen. While off window 2h June delivery cargos were reported done at June FEI plus mid-teens. On Wed a non-Us 22/22 split cargo for 2h June delivery is traded at flat price of 494$, equates to May CP plus mid low 50s, which has surprised players as initially some sellers asking at a premium of 70s for cargos sale into China. Premium has come off rapidly and a couple of cargos have been placed into China. 11/11 for 1h June delivery is reported concluded at May CP plus mid low 50s while propane a few bucks more.   Taiwan CPC issued buy tender for 22kt equal ratio cargo during 21-30 June delivery. The result is yet to know. FPC has issued buy term tender for 22-44k C3 delivered from July 2019 to June 2020.   The escalating China-Us trade tension is another focus of this week, and stock/commodity market have been very volatile. Players are cautiously waiting for official results on Friday, although most not really anticipate for a positive result according to latest reactions.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Exports from the US have maintained above 1.3million barrels per day. Market participants sees this level as the new normal at least until the EPD expansion comes on line with 7 more cargos per month in September. The arbs remain wide enough to sustain strong freight levels both to Europe and the East. South American demand continues it’s seasonal rise.   On the domestic front the build of 1.1million barrels was smaller than the expected 1.5 range though overall inventories are still over 22 million higher then this time last year. Most of the builds recently have been in the Midwest which may cause some more downward pressure there as the spread between Midwest and USGC is about 6cpg but some of the other products are 10cpg or higher. The outright price has not moved very much this week on the front with 1cpg change week on week from the high to the low. The average for the week on front month has been 58.8125-59.0625, with the high being after stats came out. Also of note the prices are at or close to the lows for the last 11 months. On the Butane front the price had largely been following crude oil and has seen a little more volatility with a weekly range on the front of 63- 66.0625 for the daily average. Volumes have been fairly lackluster on the front trades.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The US market has shifted into Spring and Summer mode leaving the fears of running out of product behind. Now the sentiment has shifted to  the discussion of can the rest of the world take all the US exports?  During the Enterprise conference call yesterday their CEO referred to how high prices create supply and low prices create demand, and the US market seems to be in the sweet spot of creating supply and demand. This,  we agree with,  and with the Mt Belvieu propane price around 40 percent of WTI, we see the arb being open and exports continuing at a very high level. In fact exports for last week were seen at record levels.  Also during the conference call  Enterprise confirmed their expansion is on schedule and additional exports will commence during the 3rd quarter of this year.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco set their May Contract Prices for Propane at $525$, up by $10 and for Butane at $530, down by $5. Although it was in line with the swap values, some players now say the contract price is higher than their expectations, more so as crude has softened this week.  Qatar Petroleum released their June acceptances with only a few delays, most lifters got dates as per nomination. June CP has seen a mini crash, so now standing at $450 at the time of writing, equal to a 14 pct drop as compared to May. Butane saw a even larger drop in prices. June CP may yet rebound, as Iran sanctions starts to take effect but so far the slow demand from India and perceived sufficient supply from US have suppressed the price.   FAR EAST:  The market is quiet due to Japan Golden Week and China Labour Day celebrations.  Few bids and offers are shown in the window, with 23kt C3 for 1h June bid at June FEI plus $13/14 and no offers seen, at the same time 2h June Sellers are asking May FEI level minus $1.  With the US terminal backlocks being slowly cleared, players anticipate that the 2h June market will be sufficiently supplied with cargoes and premiums will come off.  China imported 4.67mmt LPG in Q1, slightly less by than same period in 2018 by 2 pct, this is despite China now has one additional PDH plant which commenced operations during Feb 2019. Currently China’s domestic market price is under pressure with disappointing margins from both residential and petchem sectors is seen. In addition the summer season is soon upon us, combined with disappointing Propylene demand and lower Gasoline additives margins. Even so, China importers have started exploring the June market with expectations that premiums coming off with softening freight and overall ample supply.  China based LPG Buyers still have to cope with the uncertainty on US-China tariff talks, positive signals have been released in recent talks and people expects something progressive will come out soon.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Firstly, thanks to all readers for completing the information request sent out last week, it’s great to have such a strong response and an active audience. Enough of the admin, the LNG freight market has more than enough going on to fill this column despite numerous public holidays worldwide. Live tenders from CFE and Gail this week have caused a spur of activity in and around the Americas. Across the Atlantic, West Africa has also had its fair share of available cargoes just as the first production from Argentina looks to be hitting the market. When considered with the Algerian and Egyptian volumes seen over the recent weeks and the imminent US commissioning volumes due, the Atlantic has never been so dynamic in terms of production. It’s not quite as positive on the demand side with the Atlantic to Pacific arb struggling to support consistent cross basin trade flow. The Pacific remains a little muted with limited fixtures being reported and as we increase the ballast bonus sentiment, it is the Pacific that weighs on the assessment advancing further this week. No reported new build orders this week but some long term tenders are progressing well which should see the total tally of uncommitted vessels on order book reduce. Happy holidaying if you are out of the office this week.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Optimisation is the name of the game for those players with a fleet of LNG vessels. Portfolio players constantly optimise their fleets to charter in whenever it is more economical to do so, whilst spare vessels, usually with short term availability, are marketed for third party charter and this goes someway to explaining the number of vessels chalked up on the position list. Despite the number of chartering enquiries, rates remain depressed as competition remains high with shipowners eager to ensure that their vessels are moving. There are various cargoes available in the Pacific basin and they are set to keep chartering activity at a moderate level but some way off those previously witnessed. With new US volumes due to come online in the coming months and the hope of a warm start to summer, Owner's eyes are on charter hire rate levels with the hope of tightening in the shipping market. In reality this could be some months off but on the flip-side sublets are a high percentage of the availability and can vanish with little warning. Worldwide availability looks relatively balanced albeit oversupplied as intra-basin trade continues to be the overwhelming route choice.     The Atlantic basin has been relatively quiet of late but we expect some vessels to be fixed given the ongoing good production out of North Africa. Spot trades from the Atlantic to the Far East are still a rarity with the abundance of cargoes from South East Asia and Australia providing any Far East LNG purchase interest with an obvious choice of source for any required cargoes.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Following the rise in crude price, May CP price has surpassed April CP, now being $20 higher at 535$ at the time of writing. May/June CP is still in heavy backwardation but continues to narrow from the previous $46 to $28 within this week.  Freight has continuously soared, whereby eroding the potential CFR profits.  FOB lifters without ship length, are keen to resell their FOB’s rather than bringing the CFR volumes to the Far East themselves.  May FOB’s, especially with lifting in the last decade of May, is reported to have been concluded and mid/high single digit discounts to May CP.    FAR EAST: The rally hasn’t ended, and prices are edging up by a day by day basis. Until this Wednesday 23k propane for 1h June delivery was traded at June FEI plus $30.  Cargoes for 2h May delivery is being bid at May FEI plus $50 and no offers seen.  May FEI/CP has narrowed rapidly from minus $20 to near flattish during this week, partly because the tightness in front month for Far East market and also because positions are being rolled into June.  Until backlog delays are cleared thoroughly from US, we will likely see the Eastern tightness extending into 1h June.  Chinese importers have more or less finished their May buying program and are now looking at their June schedule. Recent deal premium levels has varied from $50’s level to $70s on May CP linkage, subject to cargo delivery time range.  PDH margins have been squeezed by higher Propane costs and weaker Propylene demand, we do however expect demand from this sector will stay stable as most units have substantial downstream linkage, yielding higher value products.  Indonesia’s Pertamina was reported to have awarded their two buy tenders on FOB basis, one middle May for lifting ex AG at May CP plus mid-single digit premium and one late May at CP minus.  FPC has awarded their buy tender for 44k propane delivered to Mailiao during 1-10 June at June MOPJ minus high 40s, with 6 offers received. Some players reckon it’s higher than expectations as compared to a window deal on the same day, while others assessed higher value for cargo delivered early June, plus higher freight costs.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: We are starting to see a clearer picture of the volume of exports lost to the delays on the Houston ship channel. Exports were curbed by approximately 200,000 barrels per day for 45 days. Keeping 9 million barrels of LPG in the domestic US market. With this in mind some traders found it surprising to see Mt Belvieu prices rise after a slightly smaller than expected, but still a build of 1 million barrels in US inventories. We expect to see maximum exports from US terminals for the next few weeks as the catch up continues,  with the normal lifting schedule to be resumed at all terminals by the beginning of June. South American demand continues its seasonal increase. Importers are having to pay hefty premiums to draw tons to the region to compete with the CFR market in the East. Regarding the Gasmar tender it is still uncertain if they were able to buy anything for second half June arrival.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: As Easter Holidays is coming closer, it is safe to say that activity is slowing down. Spot fixing interest has now shifted to May-June cargos in both basins and quite a few fixtures has been concluded already.  East of Suez, availability list has shortened significantly, rates, however, haven’t seen any drastic change so far, but Charterers should make notes.  West of Suez, availability consists mainly of sublet tonnage which means that Atlantic might at any stage become short of shipping, should those players with extra tonnage optimise their portfolios. For now, main shipping interest is related to cargoes out of the Mediterranean and should this continue, things might become more active after Easter. In Newbuilding market, Capital Gas has been reported to have exercised their second option for a vessel with HHI giving them a total of six vessels.  On a separate comment please kindly note that right after Easter we will be sending out a GDPR Form for compliance relating to our reports, and in the meantime we wish everyone a Happy Easter!

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: This week brought most of the LNG players back to the grind after last week’s meetings and networking in Shanghai. Activity seem to have “hit the ground running” with a firmer sentiment - from what could have been the lowest level of year 2019  with regards to the intensity of the LNG shipping activities. While the Chinese players dominated the showcasing of their LNG capabilities in the LNG19 conference, this week everybody joined in (traders, exporters, importers alike) and chartered vessels from all basins. This has resulted in some vessels finding the way out from their idling positions and we see a number of sublet vessels that were available, being withdrawn from our availability lists to do internal trades, further reducing the list of tonnage seeking employment.  Despite the recent activities, headline rates remain stable, but with the likelihood of improvements on the ballast bonus figures going forward. We expect full round trip economics for the shipping costs to maybe come before the headline rates improve.  On the newbuilding front, Maran Gas Maritime and NYK again have hit the headlines with both ordering yet another 174,000m3 LNG vessel respectively, with deliveries from DSME for the former and Hyundai Samho for the latter, to be ready within 2022. NYK’s order is reportedly on the back of a long term charter of up to 20 years including optional extension periods.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: ADNOC released their May acceptances with some delays reported, this was inevitable as most lifters nominated basis preferred early month lifting because of the heavy backwardation from May to June.    Qatar Petroleum is reported to have sold a May 31 to Jun 1st lifting of 46/0 at June CP plus $11-12 to a trading house. Premium for May FOB liftings varies widely pending on the different loading laycans, from mid high teens to single digits, the latter the cheaper.  At the time of writing, May Propane CP is traded at $505 and Butane assessed $15 higher, with June Propane CP is at $29 less.  Freight market ex MEG remains tight in the front month. Baltic kept it’s upward momentum up this week, which eroded the margins on delivery basis, with lifters tending to sell FOBs at premium to cash premium instead of bringing the cargo into the East themselves, unless they have their own shorts to cover.    FAR EAST: It was another hectic week with robust buying inquires, especially so for front the market against only a few offers. Although Houston channel has resumed operation, minimum 7-10 days are still expected to clear the backlock loading at some terminals.  Therefore, the front tightness extends into 2h May or even 1h June. Off window there is talk circulating that a 23k Propane cargo for delivery during 1h May traded at May FEI plus $60, while 1h/2h May swap value is at $20. On Thursday a 22/22 cargo for 1h May delivery were bid at May FEI plus $70, and bids for 23/0 for 1h May and 2h May was at May FEI plus $55 and plus $30 respectively, no offers for 1h May delivery was seen and 2h May sellers was at 10 dollars higher.  Chinese importers are also exploring cargoes for May, however limited cargoes are shown and the few that are is asking high $60ish or even higher, this is due to the higher FOB premiums and freight.   Some importers have shifted buying requirements from 1h May into 2h May, hoping they can secure cheaper cargoes, this doesn’t look to be the case yet, especially when there are outstanding trader shorts competing for the same cargoes.  Though Propylene appears weak and has squeezed PDH margins, this is unless it is an integrated downstream units.  Compared to high premium on “regular” tons, Iranian origins appear rather attractively priced and April/May imports is expected to be maintained or exceed the March volume which was at 500k tonnes.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: FOB discussions in the USGC remain thin. The fog and benzene spill caused havoc and delays which will affect USGC loadings well into May. Traders with cargoes loading from terminals on the Houston ship channel are still unsure of the exact number of days delay they will incur. Halting all FOB trade discussions in the area due to laycan uncertainty. This has led to Marcus Hook going from the ugly duckling, during the well documented ME2 commissioning problems, to the belle of the ball today. Demand for East Coast US tons is at a premium and Marcus Hook has not disappointed. Set to export 9 VLGCs in April and we believe 7 VLGCs per month onwards. Marcus Hook is having a global impact on export cargo flows. The build of 1.2 million barrels although expected surprisingly pushed MT Belvieu up to 42% WTI from 39% the week prior. Latin American demand has been strong, with 80 000 MT more imported into Mexico alone in the 1st quarter 2019 compared with 1st quarter 2018. South American incremental seasonal demand continues, a recent US VLGC tender is rumoured to be heading that way.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: LNG 19 in Shanghai is well underway and there is some exciting news being released in connection with the conference. In terms of shipping, it has been announced that TMS Cardiff secured a 10yrs contract with Vitol. In the product market Shell has signed a SPA with NextDecade for 2 MTPA from the Rio Grande project and Novatek has signed preliminary supply agreements with both Vitol and Repsol for volumes from their Arctic 2 project. With a lot of the market participants in Shanghai for LNG 19 the spot market is quiet, with only sporadic requirements surfacing. Spot rates are stable from last week, but the outlook continues to look positive.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG： Qatar Petroleum released their May acceptances with some lifters experiencing 2-3 weeks’ delays, mainly for equal ratio cargoes which were nominated for early month lifting. QP is reportedly selling a 45 kt Propane cargo for 1st decade lifting at June CP plus around $10 premium, they may still be able to squeeze a full Propane spot cargo for end May or early June loading. The Baltic VLGC freight has soared by over $5 during the last few days (WOW) and is still climbing. With limited vessels open in the East until 1st decade May.  Traders with cargo length and not enough shipping, tends to resell their FOB tons to collect the premium instead of selling CFR delivery.  Saudi Aramco announced April CP over the weekend at $515 for Propane and $535 for Butane, up by $25 and $15 respectively. Since the April CP was announced, May CP has gained quickly and is $494 at the time of writing.  However the spread between May/June CP have widened from last week’s 20ish to $40. May FEI/CP also widened from previous -$8 to -$26, which reflects the front strength against forward length.    FAR EAST: The tightness in the front market didn’t see any relief during this week.  Although the Houston ship channel slowly started to resume to normal operation, lifters are still waiting for clearance on previous backlogs.  Limited or no sellers can commit cargoes with fixed arrival until the vessel has departed from US Gulf.  23kt Propane for 1H May arrival is bid at May FEI plus $48 while the offer is at $21 higher.  22+22 kt c3/c4 cargoes is in even shorter supply with buyer’s bidding at May CP plus $60 with no sellers to be seen.  23kt Propane for 2H May arrival is less tight  with value being about $25 less.  Off window discussions mostly ended up in deadlock.  Japanese and Korean importers are not willing to release AG origin cargoes without in return getting US origin cargoes back because of low inventory.  Very few trades was concluded within this week, as a consequence inquiries are outstanding ranging from 2h April to May delivery.  Indian IOC issued a buy tender for 22+22 kt c3/c4 with 2h May delivery into Ennore, and optional parcels for 15/15 kt or 20/20 kt delivered in June to Aug.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: Mt Belvieu propane prices weakened Wednesday following a larger than expected build of 1.6 million barrels. Domestic production remains above 2 million barrels a day whilst exports were above 1 million barrels a day for the second week running. At the Houston IHS conference much of the talk has been about new US export capacity coming on at the end of this year and in 2020, aligning well with new US fractionation capacity. Both of which will be substantial. The belief is still that all of the new US propane to hit the water will find a home by pricing itself into the international market.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG： The intermonth CP value is still in a heavily backwardated structure. April/May remains at $45-50 while May/June now stands at $15-20.  At time of writing, April Propane CP is traded at 507$, and butane stands at $20 higher. Cargoes which can make within April delivery are being favored and discussed at teens premium. Freight has soared to above $40, as plenty of vessels are lining up outside US and limited tonnage showing open in the AG gulf.    FAR EAST: Front market is extremely tight, with a handful of cargoes being delayed due to the Houston ship channel closure. On Wednesday 23kt propane for 2h April arrival was traded at Apr FEI plus $50, and a similar cargo for 1h May arrival was concluded at May FEI plus $40. Some traders have continue trying to arrange time swaps to secure tons with delivery within April.  Indonesia’s Pertamina have issued tenders to secure two split-ratio cargoes for 1h May delivery, while BPCL also tendered to buy similar cargos for 1h/mid-May delivery. Results of these are yet to be known.   Most Chinese importers are exploring cargos for 1h May arrival, even so there are still some prompt inquiries for April delivery. Sellers are hesitant showing offers because of heavy backwardations.  As MEG supply is short, Chinese players have turned to some other origins. Our shiptrack shows around 500k tons Iranian origin cargoes discharge into China within the month of March, which is the highest on record in the recent past. April volume is expected to be slightly smaller as less floating cargoes are available.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The winter is over, the absolute price of propane is falling, and this combined with loading delays  is allowing the arbs and freights to reach the best levels in over a year. Delays in the US Gulf has caused near panic in Asia forcing premiums to FEI to sky rocket. The US is exporting roughly 2.5 million tons per month of LPG and out of this roughly 50 percent is going to Asia . Hence 15 day delays in loading translates into aproximately 750,000 mts per month into Asia and thus it is not hard to understand the large premiums being seen for second half May arrivals. The question going forward is, will arbs last at reasonable levels. Fog season will end but as stated before production is too strong and US propane must price to move. Already today propane is down to 45 percent of WTI and we expect it to drop further. Historically,  propane below 45 percent of WTI makes for a good Arb and frieght market.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: Despite wider uncertainty in the short term outlook of the cargo market due to oversupply, with some referencing output shutdowns as a consequence, multi-month charter rates remain buoyant.  Record imports persist into Europe not only from the US but also from Middle East and Africa which are struggling to find demand in the Middle East, China and the Far East. Despite the weak voyage length fundamentals spot levels this week have risen modestly off the latest floor and may signal the first signs of an upward trend.  Owners and Charterers will convene in Shanghai next week at the LNG19 conference with many discussions focusing the forward outlook which sees a variety of influencing factors, shut-ins, commissioning, summer cargo demand and yard prices. 2019 has plenty of variable elements to consider and it is this backdrop that appears to be fueling an array of forward views. The order-book grew again this week by 1 with the quoted price at 191M USD, a tick up from last done and likely to continue. In summary, short term fundamentals look weak but improving throughout the year with potential for huge volatility.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: The spot LNG shipping market sentiment is holding relatively flat for another week, although there were quite a few requirements surfacing this week in both basins, but their impact has been rather minimal, as there are still enough prompt ships looking to be chartered. The Pacific rates have not moved this week whereas the Atlantic rates have been adjusted to correspond with the latest reported levels. However, there is an underlying firmer tone developing and the markets may well experience an upturn further out, as we are seeing Charterers looking to secure tonnage for multi-month or even multi-year period(s) with delivery later part of the year, and the availability list for such periods has seen reductions. LNG end-users were also heard looking at purchasing a few spot cargoes, which could be positive development for the shipping markets.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: A build in US inventories when most market players expected a draw signaled an end to the domestic winter. There had been fog which reduced traffic in Houston ship channel for part of the week ending March 15th. This contributed to the 900,000 bbl build for the week. The fog season this year has been later and longer than previous years, and with more fog forecast for the weekend and Monday 25th March, we are not out of the woods yet. The reduced liftings from the US Gulf have maintained worldwide arbs. Domestic production is a shade below 2million barrels per day, and is only set to increase to new record levels throughout this year. The build coupled with a draw in US crude inventories has pushed Mt Belvieu propane as a percentage of WTI down to 46%, the lowest seen for quite some time. At this percentage of crude we expect the worldwide arbs to remain wide and demand to be strong. In South American markets seasonal imports continue to increase as winter nears.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: This winter in the US has been deified by smaller than expected draws in US inventories. This week the 1.2 million barrel draw was again lower than expected. The reason behind these lower draws has been the domestic production which has only dipped under the 2 million barrels per day a few times. Even through very cold weather for a sustained amount of time in many parts of the US the production is just too great.  This very high production is only set to increase and exports will be expected to make up for this additional production, ie product will have to be priced to move. The recent fog delays have had a large part in pushing up delivered markets with high cash diffs in the East and West windows, and is set to continue through the week. Traders right now are trying to assess how long these premiums will continue, and if they can justify paying through netback value for US FOBs. A tender from Chile was heard to be won on a delivered basis at around 17cpg.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: April CP swap’s have seen volatility throughout this week with $10 up and down swings on daily basis, reflecting continued uncertainty in the front market and differing views with regard to future CP value.  April MEG liftings continue being traded at double digits premium to CP and still inquires remain outstanding. Spurred by demand from India and Indonesia especially.  Term lifters are still awaiting Saudi acceptances, which should come over the weekend, before taking additional decisions.  At the time of writing, April propane CP is traded at $488 and butane at around $20 higher.  FAR EAST: There is big a big gap in price between cargoes delivered in 1h April versus 2h April. This Thursday 23kt propane for 2h Apr was concluded at balance March FEI flat, and other bids for similar cargo are at April FEI plus $12.  However, the CFR market for 1h April delivery continue being very active, with bidding at April FEI +$34 while offering stands at April CP +$47, this equates to April FEI plus $60 at current values.  The delays of US origin tonnes saw no relief this week, causing further backwadation between 1st and 2nd half arrival cargoes.  India’s BPCL issued buy tenders totaling 85kt in total volume for April delivery. Indonesia’s Pertamina tendered to buy a 44kt split cargo for delivery in 1h April, the result is unknown at time of writing. FPC withdrew their buy tender for 22k or 44k propane for delivery 6-20 April as no suitable offer was received for this period.  A couple of propane and heavy propane cargos have been sold into China, with premium concluded reported to be above April CP +$40’s.  There are still outstanding inquires for 2h April delivery but buyer’s sentiment is weaker because of slow domestic distribution and eroding margins with surging costs.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: FOB cargoes on sale across all basins, plus some short term requirements have kept things bit more busy this week, especially as we move towards the shoulder months. In the spot market, the scenery has however not changed significantly and the availability list yet remains long, giving Charterers plenty of options. Therefore, spot rates remain under pressure across all three basins. In the term market, however, interest from Charterers in securing tonnage towards autumn/winter has increased and especially for coverage from September onwards.  For a change, there were no new large LNGC  orders reported this week, but plenty activity on SSLNG, a segment we also follow closely here at Fearnleys.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: We’ve noticed a small increase in fixture activity from the past few weeks, but the charter levels are in line with shoulder season expectations. Shipping rates, both in the West and in the East were somewhat soft and we’ve logged a small reduction on the spot headliner rates. On a positive note there isn’t too much downside risk left in the spot market and «Owners» continues to be optimistic about 3Q and the winter to come. Vessel availability has come off slightly, but not enough to have an impact yet on spot rates. We kept LNG newbuild prices stable this week, but shipyards are reporting good interest in LNG slots.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: The Mt Belvieu market took Wednesday’s draw of 2 million barrels in US inventories in its stride. The arbs to Asia and Europe remain very strong, with high premiums in the respective windows. These have been pushing up US FOB offer levels. We could even see double figures for a March cargo if one becomes available. Fog in the US Gulf has played it’s part in delaying laycans, pushing up the prompt window premiums as vessels get delayed. Another 4 straight days of fog are expected over the weekend, potentially delaying more loadings. Terminals are doing their best to clear any backlog and mitigate as much fog risk as possible. A US Gulf Coast FOB tender for up to a cargo a month from May to December 2019 was released this week. With market participants agreeing that it was a good time to release a tender with wide arbs. It was a bit of surprise when an Eastern trader released another USGC FOB tender for a cargo per month from April to September 2019. In South America, Gasmar issued a tender to buy CFR into Chile for end April arrival. This marked the beginning of the demand season in the region as the Southern Hemisphere transitions into winter.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: It all started middle of the week, April CP moved from $460 to $490s. Tightness in the front market have pushed up the price. Saudi Aramco appear to have little to nothing when it come to spot availabilities till June. Term lifters are cautiously waiting for April lifting acceptances, also thinking about confirmed and possible future   US fog delays. The spread between Propane and Butane has narrowed a bit with anticipation that more US butane will come to East. There are however some uncertainties due to the weather.   FAR EAST: The Asian market has been quiet with the Tokyo conference being this week.  Nevertheless, in the window one Korean importer aggressively bid for 23kt propane for prompt 2h Mar delivery. No sellers appeared in the window until Thursday, to offer 23kt propane for 1h April, this show a premium of low 40s over April CP.  April CP gained strength from the tightness in front month, with April FEI less support. With expectation that ample supply from US will sail to east, Apr FEI/CP turned into negative again and traded at minus $8 at the time of writing.   Off window there are active inquiries from either China or SEA. But with slim margins in both residential and PDH petchem, importers might restrain their spot activities and cover volume on rigid demand basis. Indonesian Pertamina is reported to have awarded their last tender for 11/11 only arriving early April. Another noticeable phenomenon is more Iranian cargoes have been tracked sailing to China from Mar. So far we’ve seen around 300k tonnes is arriving/will arrive in first half period.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
x: MEG: Saudi Aramco announced Mar CP at $490 and $520 respectively for propane and butane, up by $50 each, which is much higher than player’s expectation. The tightness on AG spot supply didn't get relieved and traders can scarcely squeeze out tons for resale. Apr CP swap is heavily backwardated, but slowly edged up at $466 at the time of writing. Apr C3/C4 spread has narrowed down from Mar at $20 at the time being.  FAR EAST: Tightness in 2h Mar extends into 1h Apr. The foggy weather in US continues and incurs further delays, which exert upward pressures on price in short term. On Wed a 23kt propane delivered in 1h Apr was traded at Apr FEI plus $15, which is $12$ higher than other bid. And we barely see any offers for this period even off window. 2h Apr is slightly at ease with expectation that the cargo will move smooth later on. Price of non-US origin is also hitting rooftops, with outstanding tenders from Indian and Indonesia for equal ratio cargoes delivered ranged from late Mar to Apr. Propane cargo within Mar arrival is reported done at low mid 40s into China, and premium of for 1h Apr arrival cargos hover over 40$. One North China petchem user has issued a private tender to secure one full propane cargo delivered in Apr. And other Chinese are actively inquired for propane or heavy propane cargo delivered in 1h Apr as well.

t: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
n: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
x: This winter in North America has been a monster. The cold weather started early and it has lasted long. None the less the propane production has been an even bigger monster. Averaging just over 2 million barrels a day, the question of whether the US could handle record exports and cold weather has been answered with a resounding YES. Export Terminals and mid-stream companies are gearing up with expansions, new fractionators, and new pipelines to handle the production going forward, but the question will no longer be is there enough product,  but where will the product go? This week US C3 inventories decreased by 1.2 million barrels which was less than expectations. This and declining freight rates has allowed the arb to widen to levels not seen in several months and is pointing towards stronger terminalling fees. It certainly seems that this who locked in terminalling under 6 cpg for 2019 are currently on the right side for now.

n: LNG Market Report
x: We are almost done and dusted with February and that also means the official end of the Northern Hemisphere “winter months”. From a market perspective there is little change, as the cargo demand has stayed relatively flat for a while now. There are however signs of improved cargo activity, which has in turn rippled into new shipping requirements for March and April. Still, LNGC spot rates remain under pressure, since the availability list is rather long and includes sublets that in general can fix at competitive levels to compensate for their reduced flexibility or period availability.  It’s IP week in London, and among other discussions, there are still a wide range of views on how the rest of the 2019 will pan out on commodity pricing. The only thing certain is that no one has a reliable crystal ball.  On the newbuilding side, it was another active week with Maran Gas ordering two more 174,000cbm LNGC newbuilds from DSME for late 2021 delivery. More to come next week?

n: LNG Market Report
x: Amid the bearish sentiments circulating since the start of the month, we did see improvements in terms of shipping requirements this week.  Activity has picked up and mainly in the East of Suez. However, spot shipping rates are still under pressure as demand is unable to support the current number of vessels available. Furthermore, we have seen a continuous dip in the Far East LNG prices, which in turn continues to keep the West-to-East arbitrage opportunities low. Going forward, and as we are about to enter the “shoulder months” in the gas market, the market expects current shipping levels to remain relatively flat. However, as the current spot market is in favour towards the Charterers, we may start seeing more interest for multi-month requirements to cover the second half of the year and the next winter. On newbuildings, we understand that Maran Gas has exercised their option and has placed another order for a 174,000cbm MEGI with DSME. Reports indicate that the vessel will be delivered in the first half of 2021.
