t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: IOC terminal commissioning was hotly contended this week and is welcome demand and marks the opening of the first LNG Terminal on the East coast of India. This new arrival occurs just as OLT announces that the LNG Toscana Regasification Terminal in Italy is working at almost 100% after less than one year from the introduction of the new allocation mechanism via auction, a very clear indication that trade routes has shifted significantly. Signs of Spring can be seen in Europe which is welcome relief from the dark days of winter but offers less rest bite for owners. The position list could be described as blossoming but that doesn’t give correct connotations for its effect on the market and charter rates which continue to soften. Its weak across the board – all basins and all duration take a hit except for 3 years and longer. Its clear that the prompt market is being underpinned but lackluster demand but the bigger picture remains relatively stable, more LNG due to be produced, the only question mark here is will it be in time for winter 2019/2020. Second-hand prices and NB prices remain stable, for now, but ongoing discussions between the Korean yards could see a significant change in the ownership structure of the 1st tier LNG yards, which may impact NB prices and in turn Charter rates.

x: LNG spot market activity remains muted as Lunar New Year festivities take place in most parts of Asia Pacific and with no arbitrage between the basins. Rates are continuing their descending trend on the back of limited requirements in all basins. In the East, availability keeps growing and although it would seem as a better place to be for an Owner, a few independent Owners are repositioning their open vessels to the Atlantic. In the West, availability is slowly growing as Independent Owners’ positions are joining the existing available sublets. But as a few projects will be commissioning cargoes during Q2, some more activity is indeed expected in the US Gulf. On other news, it is very encouraging for the LNG market to see another major US project getting its FID – Congratulations to the Golden Pass promoters. Yards may continue to be busy building LNG vessels. Second hand prices remain stable and there were no Newbuilding transactions recorded this week.  In the meantime, we wish everyone a Happy Lunar New Year!!

x: The shipping market continues to mark time and sentiment shifts to the downside. Pacific and Atlantic rate levels have continued their downward trajectory throughout the week despite the market seeing a pickup in vessel requirements, the impact on availability? Minimal as there are plenty of open ships.    Looking ahead, the market may see an upturn after the celebrations of Chinese New Year. Until then, the vessel availability list looks likely to continue to lengthen. In the Middle East, the odd requirement can be witnessed whilst in the Atlantic, portfolio players remain well serviced by vessels delivering into Europe, that said, there is interest from parties with specific needs. Turning to the Pacific, it looks mildly more optimistic for Owners, yet requirements fall short of the number of vessels sitting prompt and it’s probably fair to say idle time will mount up as requirements turn their focus to second half-Feb or even March.   Second hand prices remain flat as do New Build prices as we welcome two new high spec, fuel efficient vessels scheduled for delivery in 2021.

n: LNG Market Report
x: Another week of a relatively soft shipping market as the lack of intensity in trading activities has led to various project and trader-controlled vessels being available for sub-let. This is in addition to vessels being redelivered this and next month due to charterers not declaring the optional periods, where they had previously anticipated an active trading market in January. As a result the current sentiment is far from what most have predicted a couple of months ago.  Every fixture heard in the market recently seems to have been done at terms lower than the previous fixture as headline rates dropped approximately 70% since the peak levels established in November. As reported last week, the correlation between the LNG shipping and cargo market has been restored but It may not take long for vessel availability to drop significantly as soon as there is an uptick of trading activities. As project and trader-controlled vessels contribute to almost half of the available tonnage list, expect these ships to be the first to go, to be utilized by their own charterers when LNG trading and demand increases.

t: LNG Market Report
n: LNG Market Report
x: We are half-way to January and it does feel like the shipping market has taken a breather. We are only seeing limited new activity, which together with a number of redeliveries East of Suez, has caused our short term availability to look rather long, especially in the Pacific. As a result, any new piece of shipping business has gained great interest from the Owners, which has consequently put pressure on rates. As a matter of fact, it is starting to look like the correlation between the LNG shipping and cargo market has restored, making it more challenging to see any change in the short term shipping sentiment without a boost in the cargo side first (more cargoes or better arb’s). Although we are in the winter months, we get the feeling that without a solid cold spike, the “shoulder month season” might be coming upon us sooner than expected. That said, as we have learned in the past, the tide can change very quickly in the world of LNG and the players who can move just before the tidal change, will usually get the best deals.  For a change, the shipyards had a rather quiet announcement week as no new LNGC orders were reported.

x: The first proper trading week of 2019 is underway and although we’ve recorded a good number of fixtures so far this year, it hasn’t been enough the get the shipping market out of the softening trend we’ve seen through the holiday season. The shipping rates have come off and so has other elements such as the ballast bonus sentiment. This weakening can mostly be associated to an increase in availability, amongst which, some are sublets, which indicates that the underlying demand is also coming off. Although the spot market is coming off near term, the sentiment and Owners remain optimistic for 2019 and term rates for a 1yr and 3yrs TC’s are relatively stable.

x: While many of the market participants are still enjoying the Festive Period, market activity has just slowly started to pick up. A few fresh requirements, one from an Eastern Major, will keep things busy this week, but as vessel availability in the East is increased, it will not be a surprise if we witness a further correction on East of Suez rates as Charterers are focusing on February cargoes. In the Atlantic, availability is limited and consists mainly of portfolio sublet tonnage as activity remains muted and with the West to East arbitrage closed it will be interesting to see the next market direction here. On the newbuild front, a few more orders were added just as we got into the festive mode. A record high 60 LNG vessels were ordered in 2018. Will this activity continue in 2019? As this is just the first week of the year, we expect more activity to emerge as we move ahead and we looking forward to a great year for LNG in 2019! Wishing you all a Happy New Year!
